a_rows_sample.anchor: Hertz and Thomson agreed on the observed result — no electrical deflection was detected — but disagreed about whether that observation constituted evidence for electrical neutrality. Thomson later showed that the experimental setup itself was inadequate ... Observation ≠ Evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Central finding: evidence collection is itself a domain, not mere ingestion; Achinstein's Hertz/Thomson example (same observed non-deflection, disputed evidential status, later traced to inadequate evacuation causing a screening effect) establishes Observation != Evidence, refining the naive System->collect->store->AI-analyzes->knowledge pipeline into Observation -> Candidate evidence -> Evidence assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceAcquisition: Question, Hypothesis, TargetPopulation, SelectionProcedure, ObservationMethod, MeasurementMethod, Conditions, Instrumentation, SamplingRules, Exclusions, Competitors, ExpectedObservations, Result. The evidence is the result of an acquisition process.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes EvidenceAcquisition as a new core concept distinct from Evidence itself, with a lifecycle Question->Design acquisition->Acquire observation->Validate observation->Assess selection->Assess flaws->Create candidate evidence, and tentatively identifies an Evidence Acquisition Context as a candidate (not yet certified) bounded context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Achinstein explicitly rejects the simplistic idea that simply accumulating many observations automatically gives evidence. ... Evidence Quality ≠ Quantity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence Quality is not Quantity: a large observation set can be epistemically weak under a biased selection mechanism; decomposes Evidence Quality (as an architectural decomposition, explicitly not a literal formula) into observation quality x selection quality x measurement quality x context adequacy x explanatory relevance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: insufficient evacuation -> gas conductivity -> screening -> no observable deflection. ... MeasurementContext: instrument, configuration, calibration, environment, resolution, detection limits, operating conditions, known failure modes.
a_rows_sample.statement: Measurement must also be treated as an acquisition mechanism: the Hertz/Thomson case shows a hidden instrumentation flaw (insufficient evacuation causing screening) suppressing an observation; proposes a MeasurementContext object, described as 'an epistemic measurement contract.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation: What happened? Acquisition: How did we obtain knowledge of what happened? Evidence claim: Why does this observation support this hypothesis? ... They must not collapse into one entity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence collection has three distinct objects that must not collapse: Observation (what happened), Acquisition (how knowledge of it was obtained), and Evidence claim (why the observation supports a hypothesis).

a_rows_sample.anchor: his 'Michael Jordan eats Wheaties' example illustrates that something can have high probability given a fact without that fact actually providing a reason for the hypothesis; there must be an explanatory connection. ... True observation ≠ Decision-relevant evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Wisdom Lens: not every true observation is decision-relevant evidence -- Achinstein's high-probability-without-explanatory-connection example ('Michael Jordan eats Wheaties') motivates an EvidenceRelevance check asking whether an observation actually bears on the claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An acquisition cannot be declared completed-for-evidence until the procedure, conditions, observations and deviations are recorded sufficiently to permit epistemic assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposed EvidenceAcquisition aggregate (EvidenceQuestion, TargetClaim, TargetPopulation, SelectionProcedure, MeasurementPlan, AcquisitionConditions, AlternativeExplanations, ObservationProtocol, Observations, Deviations, AcquisitionAssessment) with the candidate aggregate invariant that completion-for-evidence requires sufficiently recorded procedure/conditions/observations/deviations, explicitly flagged as a candidate domain model, not yet for implementation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Achinstein explicitly rejects the idea that evidence must always be newly predicted. Known/old observations can still function as evidence depending on the circumstances. ... Evidence is contextualized observation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces EvidenceObservation as distinct from Observation because an observation collected for operational reasons (e.g. a 2026-08-24 production incident) may only later become relevant evidence for a new hypothesis; 'Evidence is contextualized observation' -- the same observation can be evidence for one hypothesis and irrelevant to another; grounded in Achinstein's rejection of the old-evidence-can't-count view.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Book of Evidence tells us HOW observations become evidence ... Causal Inference tells us HOW evidence supports causal claims ... Statistical methods tell us HOW evidence is quantified ... DDD tells us HOW to model the domain ... Wisdom tells us HOW to determine what evidence is needed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines all four books+lenses into one epistemic operating loop: Decision -> Evidence Need -> Evidence Question -> Acquisition Design -> {Selection Procedure, Measurement Procedure, Context Conditions} -> Observation -> Acquisition Audit -> Candidate Evidence -> Evidence Assessment -> Statistical Analysis -> Causal Assessment -> Knowledge -> Wisdom -> Decision, described as 'starting to look like the actual KnowledgeOS epistemic operating loop.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL distinguish observation acquisition from evidential interpretation. The mechanism by which an observation is selected, generated, measured and contextualized SHALL be preserved because the evidential status and strength of an observation may depend on that acquisition procedure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records as a research finding the SHALL-level principle separating observation acquisition from evidential interpretation, with its rationale explicitly grounded in Achinstein's Hertz, raven and drug examples.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI agents should not be allowed to collect 'supporting evidence' without an acquisition strategy. ... That should become part of the future KnowledgeOS Agent Developer Guide.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a required AI-agent evidence-collection procedure (clarify hypothesis -> identify evidence need -> identify competing explanations -> define selection criteria -> collect candidate observations -> record provenance -> audit selection -> assess evidence -> conclusion) replacing naive claim->web-search->supporting-documents->answer behavior, flagged for a future KnowledgeOS Agent Developer Guide.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Evidence Acquisition & Provenance ... Q1 What exactly is an Observation? ... Q14 How does Wisdom determine which evidence acquisition has the highest decision value?
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a dedicated 'KnowledgeOS Evidence Acquisition & Provenance' research/discovery round (explicitly declining to jump to implementation) with 14 open questions covering Observation vs Evidence, EvidenceNeed, SelectionProcedure, AcquisitionProcedure, MeasurementContext, alternative-explanation representation, selection-bias detection, acquisition-deviation recording, observation-to-candidate-evidence promotion, evidence validation, entry into causal inference, detecting when more evidence is needed, and Wisdom's determination of highest-decision-value acquisition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The architecture should probably not begin: Evidence Repository. It should begin: EVIDENCE NEED -> EVIDENCE ACQUISITION -> OBSERVATION -> EVIDENCE STATUS -> KNOWLEDGE. ... evidence claims are themselves empirical and can depend on facts about how evidence was generated.
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes KnowledgeOS should not primarily ask 'what evidence do we have?' but rather 'given what we are trying to know or decide, what evidence do we need, how should we obtain it, how do we know the acquisition is trustworthy, and when is the resulting observation entitled to count as evidence?' -- reordering the architecture to start from EvidenceNeed rather than an Evidence Repository, grounded in the claim that evidence claims are themselves empirical (Thomson's discovery of the Hertz flaw as the clearest demonstration).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence acquisition is the deliberate creation or retrieval of observations under explicit conditions, procedures, relationships and purposes such that the resulting observations can subsequently be assessed for their relevance and reliability with respect to a claim or decision. ... not 'is automatically evidence.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Deeper formal definition of evidence acquisition, emphasizing the phrase 'can subsequently be assessed' as distinct from 'is automatically evidence' -- an explicit correction/refinement of the prior file's treatment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: REALITY -> occurs -> PHENOMENON -> encounter/detection -> OBSERVATION -> acquisition context -> OBSERVATION RECORD -> assessment -> CANDIDATE EVIDENCE -> relation to hypothesis -> EVIDENCE -> synthesis -> KNOWLEDGE -> judgement -> WISDOM -> ACTION ... plus SITUATION{PERSON/TIME/RELATION -> ROLE/CHANGE/CONTEXT} feeding OBSERVATION.
a_rows_sample.statement: Combines the Zero-Lens occurrence-to-action chain with the Chinese relational structure, concluding 'the observation is never epistemically naked' -- every observation is fed by Situation{Person/Role, Time/Change, Relation/Context}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence is not a thing that KnowledgeOS merely stores. Evidence is a status that an observation may acquire through a defensible relationship between phenomenon, observation, acquisition procedure, situation, hypothesis and explanation. ... An observation cannot be fully understood apart from the situation, relationships, conditions and transformations through which it arose.
a_rows_sample.statement: Two culminating principles: evidence is a status an observation may acquire through a defensible relationship among phenomenon/observation/acquisition procedure/situation/hypothesis/explanation (substantially stronger than 'evidence has provenance'); and an observation cannot be fully understood apart from the situation/relationships/conditions/transformations through which it arose -- so the epistemic object is Evidence + arising conditions + acquisition path + relational context + transformation history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: we should conduct a dedicated Evidence Acquisition Discovery Round ... using the two lenses ... Then we can derive the Evidence Acquisition domain model from first principles, rather than prematurely inventing entities such as EvidenceAcquisition, EvidenceNeed, or EvidenceTrajectory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes by deferring schema design: proposes a discovery round applying Zero/Chinese/Achinstein/Causal/Wisdom lenses in sequence to derive the Evidence Acquisition domain model from first principles, explicitly warning against prematurely inventing entities such as EvidenceAcquisition, EvidenceNeed, or EvidenceTrajectory -- i.e. against the very objects this file and its predecessor just proposed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Acquisition method is literally a component of the member. So the retention requirement... is already law... whether acquisition method constitutes evidential status... is a further claim law does not make. Session 1's classification is wrong for the retention claim and right for the constitutive one. Split accordingly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Session 1's classification of "the acquisition procedure itself determines whether an observation can function as evidence" as NOT ADDRESSED: law's EvidenceLinks member already carries acquisition method plus reliability conditions, with "pseudo-evidence never admitted" as a gate condition, so the retention claim (acquisition provenance preserved alongside the reference) is already law; what remains genuinely unaddressed is the constitutive claim -- whether acquisition method determines (not merely records) evidential standing, i.e. whether two identical observations could differ in standing purely because of how they were obtained.

a_rows_sample.anchor: acquisition may be its own bounded context (C -- surrounding architecture) while remaining outside the Kernel's extent (A -- no change). "Not a Kernel responsibility" and "a domain in its own right" are then both true, of different things. Classification: DISSOLVES -- DIFFERENT SCOPE LEVEL (bounded context vs Kernel extent). Tenth dissolution, tenth mechanism.
a_rows_sample.statement: Dissolves the apparent tension between S1-F011 (excludes Evidence Acquisition as a Kernel mechanism -- "the domain admits evidence, but does not acquire it") and S1-F030 (proposes acquisition as its own domain): applying an A/B/C/E extent-vs-surrounding-architecture classification, acquisition can be its own bounded context (C) while remaining entirely outside the Kernel's extent (A) -- "not a Kernel responsibility" and "a domain in its own right" are both true of different scope levels, not contradictory; the tenth dissolution found via a distinct mechanism (scope-level separation) in the review series. Explicitly flagged as an HPA-supplied classification instrument, not corpus evidence -- nothing is corroborated by applying it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is always a complementary side: supporting observation vs contradicting observation ... a serious Evidence Acquisition process should actively collect both sides. ... EvidenceInquiry: SupportingObservations, ContradictingObservations, MissingObservations, AlternativeExplanations, ContextualConditions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Yin-Yang lens: evidence acquisition should have a built-in polarity, actively seeking both observations that illuminate a hypothesis and observations that could undermine it, rather than only 'find evidence for H'; formalized as an EvidenceInquiry object; noted as compatible with Achinstein's competing-explanations requirement and with causal inference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Someone asks the question, chooses the measurement, selects the sample, interprets the result, decides whether the result is sufficient, acts upon it. ... WHO ... not simply as an identity field, but as: ROLE, AUTHORITY, RESPONSIBILITY, PURPOSE.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confucian lens: the observer's role/authority/responsibility/purpose (not merely identity) must be preserved, illustrated by contrasting a security-engineer/independent-auditor compliance observation with the same observation made by a marketing team for marketing material, which carries a different epistemic context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This does NOT mean 'trust the person'. ... The role and relationship of the observer are themselves part of the situation that must be known.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit correction guarding against misreading the Confucian observer-role lens as 'trust the person': the observer's role/relationship is itself part of the knowable situation, not a substitute for evidence, and this is stated to be compatible with Achinstein's claim that evidence statements can depend on empirical facts about the epistemic situation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The AI should not primarily be an evidence collector. It should be an Epistemic Inquiry Assistant. ... Only then: collect / search / measure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes AI's role from evidence collector to 'Epistemic Inquiry Assistant' whose job is to ask what we're trying to know, how something was observed, what was selected/excluded, what the situation was, what changed, what would contradict the claim, what alternatives exist, what remains unknown, and what evidence would reduce uncertainty -- only afterward collecting/searching/measuring; extended into an agent workflow (Question->Inquiry Formulation->Evidence Need->Acquisition Design->Collection->Provenance Capture->Selection Audit->Contradiction Search->Alternative Explanation->Evidence Assessment->Knowledge Update) that a Verification Engine should confirm was not bypassed.

a_aliases: evidence collection is itself a domain

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'evidence-inquiry-object' POSSIBLY relates to 'evidence-acquisition-domain' (batch B0012). Note: Yin-Yang-lens reframing of evidence collection as inherently two-sided: SupportingObservations, ContradictingObservations, MissingObservations, AlternativeExplanations, ContextualConditions must all be actively sought, not only observations that support a hypothesis; expanded later in the file into a fuller EvidenceInquiry object with Question/Claim/Decision Context/Target Phenomenon/Acquisition Intent/Selection Procedure/Observation Procedure/Measurement Context/Observer{identity,role,authority}/Situation{time,environment,actors,constraints}/Expected/Contradicting/Alternative/Deviations/Resulting Observations.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Logical omniscience: The system believes all logical consequences ... computationally intractable and cognitively unrealistic. ... four-valued situations: True only, False only, Both, Neither. ... Beliefs are not closed under implication. ... {Bp,B(p\supset q),
eg Bq} ... {Bp,B
eg p,
eg Bq} inconsistent beliefs without omniscience
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the B (explicit belief) operator using four-valued situations (true-only/false-only/both/neither) to avoid logical omniscience -- beliefs are not closed under implication or consequence, exemplified by satisfiable sets {Bp,B(p⊃q),¬Bq} and inconsistent-without-explosion {Bp,B¬p,¬Bq}; a first-order variant interprets existential quantification constructively, making existential generalization fail (not |= B(P(a)∨P(b))⊃B∃xP(x)); complexity results range from co-NP-complete (propositional) to undecidable (first-order with existential generalization).

type_signature.domain: formula phi, epistemic state e, situation s

a_rows_sample.anchor: EOC = Explicit Only-knowing with Complete introspection ... Mark terms that appear within modal operators with triangle. Teach(father(tom),sara)\land\neg B Teach(father(tom)^\triangle,sara) ... Decidability: first-order with unrestricted equality Undecidable.
a_rows_sample.statement: EOC logic extends B with nested beliefs, only-knowing, and equality, introducing a triangle-marking device to solve quantifying-in with explicit belief (marking terms evaluated at substitution time versus modal-operator time); catalogues decidability results ranging from O(nm) propositional to undecidable first-order-with-unrestricted-equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation: Integrate the book's findings into KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2, particularly: 1. The TELL/ASK framework -> Core operations 2. The Representation Theorem -> Sat semantics 3. Only-knowing -> Zero definition 4. Explicit belief (B) -> Tractable reasoning 5. Successor state axioms -> delta semantics 6. The triangle operator -> Quantifying-in with explicit belief
a_rows_sample.statement: Final unhedged recommendation to integrate six findings directly into Theory v1.2 (TELL/ASK->core operations, Representation Theorem->Sat semantics, Only-knowing->Zero definition, Explicit belief B->tractable reasoning, successor-state axioms->delta semantics, triangle operator->quantifying-in), without the [PROP]/[OPEN] hedging used by the more disciplined reviews elsewhere in this batch (e.g. S2520-S2524, S2526-S2528).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contr: Four-valued semantics handles contradiction without collapse. We should mark this SUPPORTING EVIDENCE ONLY. ... our own KR-CONTR-FDE experiments already showed FDE is insufficient by itself. ... Four-valued belief \neq Contr and B/N \neq Zero remain intact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Directly contradicts S2532's claim that four-valued semantics 'handles contradiction without collapse' for Contr, citing the project's own prior KR-CONTR-FDE experiment result that FDE's four values cannot distinguish all required boundary reasons (whereas Standing x Boundary x Context x Provenance did); concludes Four-valued belief != Contr and B/N != Zero remain intact -- the book independently strengthens motivation for non-classical/bounded belief representation but does not resolve Contr semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 3: What Must Be Corrected ... ASK -> Sat(K_t,r) Reject ... TELL -> Adding requirements to R_t Reject ... Only-Knowing = Zero Reject ... Four-valued semantics solves Contr Reject ... Successor-state axioms define delta Reject ... Levesque & Lakemeyer = KnowledgeOS theory Reject
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the six overclaim-rejections scattered across S2534 into one authoritative correction table: ASK!=Sat(K_t,r), TELL!=requirements-addition, Only-Knowing!=Zero, four-valued-semantics-does-not-solve-Contr, successor-state-axioms-do-not-define-delta, Levesque&Lakemeyer!=KnowledgeOS-theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **Can contradiction be represented without confusing it with uncertainty, absence, insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness, unobservability, or non-assessment?**
b_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-CONTR-2026-09: mission is to determine whether contradiction can be represented without collapsing into uncertainty/absence/insufficient-evidence/theory-incompleteness/unobservability/non-assessment, whether the current 3-valued domain is expressive enough, what the minimum evaluation domain must contain, whether a 4th value C is actually necessary, and whether contradiction has kernel implications.

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **Do not start from the assumption that KnowledgeOS needs a fourth truth value.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the single governing constraint on the experiment: it must discover the minimum required representation rather than confirm a predetermined four-valued design; possible outcomes explicitly include three values sufficient, four necessary, more than four necessary, a structured domain, contradiction belonging outside Sat, or the question needing reformulation.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
Contr(p,K_t)
\iff
Pos(p,K_t)\land Neg(p,K_t).
$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an initial (non-final) formal definition of contradiction: Contr(p,Kt) iff Pos(p,Kt) AND Neg(p,Kt), where Pos/Neg mean p/not-p is represented/committed to in the epistemic state; explicitly to be tested against provenance, confidence, temporal, source, context, retraction, supersession, coexistence, and conflicting-observation/interpretation/model differences.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
World
\neq
Observation
\neq
Evidence
\neq
Interpretation
\neq
EpistemicState
\neq
Evaluation
\neq
KnowledgeAttribution.
$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the experiment to preserve a seven-layer non-collapse chain (World≠Observation≠Evidence≠Interpretation≠EpistemicState≠Evaluation≠KnowledgeAttribution) and forbids giving the simulated agent access to hidden ground truth: Contr(p,Kt) must not mean 'the world makes both p and not-p true' but that the epistemic representation simultaneously contains incompatible commitments about p.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ## Candidate A — Fourth value ... ## 6. CANDIDATE B — Delegate contradiction to consistency ... # 7. CANDIDATE C — Exclusive construction ... # 8. CANDIDATE D — STRUCTURED EVALUATION
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the four candidate representations to test fairly: A) extend {T,F,U} to {T,F,U,C}, testing whether C is primitive/derivable/needs provenance or polarity/can coexist with U; B) keep Sat in {T,F,U} and represent Contr(p,K) as an independent relation outside Sat; C) exclusive-by-construction (bot ≡ not-p∈K ∧ p∉K), explicitly flagged as expected-vulnerable to silently converting contradictory into false/absent/invalid; D) a structured EVal=(value,reason,provenance,evidence,context,time,polarity) tuple whose exact fields must be discovered by reduction.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\forall (x,y)\in\mathcal R_{req},
\quad
x\neq y
\Rightarrow
R(x)\neq R(y).
$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy for this experiment: a candidate representation R:S->D is adequate iff for every required distinction pair (x,y) in R_req, x≠y implies R(x)≠R(y); a structured representation may satisfy this even when two conditions share the same primary 'value' field, so uniqueness of the primary value is not required.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Case 1 — Unknown ... ### Case 15 — Model conflict
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 15-case deterministic adversarial suite: unknown, absent, not-assessed, insufficient evidence, underdetermined, unobservable, direct contradiction, conflicting sources, conflicting observations, unequal-confidence contradiction, retraction, supersession, different contexts, different times, and model conflict -- each with an expected semantic condition and an instruction not to prejudge borderline cases (e.g. source conflict vs epistemic contradiction, retraction should not automatically create contradiction).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Contradiction + insufficient evidence
Contradiction + different provenance
Contradiction + temporal separation
Contradiction + context separation
Contradiction + high/low confidence
Contradiction + supersession
Contradiction + retraction
Contradiction + model disagreement
Contradiction + unobservable
Contradiction + not-assessed
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires second-order adversarial tests combining contradiction with each of ten other conditions, to discover whether C is one unitary state or has internal structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Test whether:

$$
Contradiction \Rightarrow Zero
$$

or:

$$
Contradiction \not\Rightarrow Zero
$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the Zero-interaction question as genuinely open: does contradiction imply Zero, does it not, or does contradiction require its own separate Zero classification -- to be decided by evidence, not assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
> Zero examines what the current representation does not adequately represent.

Therefore investigate whether... `ZeroLens(K_t)` can expose `contradiction` without becoming `Contradiction = Zero`
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires testing whether ZeroLens can expose contradiction without collapsing into identifying contradiction with Zero itself; a contradiction may be fully represented (hence not a representational absence) while still creating an unresolved requirement -- these are different questions that must not be conflated.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
But external mathematical systems are **research references only**. Tag them:

```text
[EXT]
```

Do not import their semantics automatically.
b_rows_sample.statement: Permits investigating Belnap four-valued semantics, paraconsistent semantics, Kleene semantics, Priest-style approaches and bilattice structures, but only as tagged [EXT] research references never automatically imported; the governing question is what KnowledgeOS empirically/formally requires, not which existing logic to adopt -- any useful external logic must have its mapping explicitly demonstrated.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Suppose:

$$
R=(v,r,p,e,c,t,s).
$$

Test removal of each component.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the minimality procedure: for a structured representation R=(value,reason,provenance,evidence,context,time,status), test removing each field individually (R_-f); if removal collapses a required distinction, f is empirically necessary for the tested representation (not universally necessary) -- an experimental minimality result only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Positive capability test ... ### Negative separation test ... ### Completeness test ... ### Minimality test
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against vacuous success: a candidate must not pass merely because all contradictory cases collapse to U (if the oracle requires contradiction stay distinct) nor because everything is classified C (which preserves contradiction while destroying all other distinctions); requires four separate tests -- positive capability, negative separation, completeness, and minimality.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
Representation
\neq
Responsibility
\neq
Evaluation
\neq
Governance.
$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires distinguishing Representation, Responsibility, Evaluation, and Governance: representing contradiction does not imply the kernel must resolve it; detecting contradiction does not imply resolving it; resolving contradiction does not imply determining truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
> Does contradiction introduce a genuinely irreducible kernel capability?

Test whether contradiction handling can be expressed through existing candidate powers such as: Observe, Interpret, Represent, Relate, Discriminate, Hypothesize, DetectGap, Challenge, Validate, Revise, Determine, Select, Qualify
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the kernel-irreducibility question: must contradiction be added to the kernel as a new operator, or can it be derived through existing candidate powers (Observe/Interpret/Represent/Relate/Discriminate/Hypothesize/DetectGap/Challenge/Validate/Revise/Determine/Select/Qualify)? Explicitly notes the outcome may be 'contradiction is a semantic state' rather than 'a kernel operator', and that this distinction is mandatory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### NEG-1 ... A fourth value `C` cannot distinguish important subtypes of contradiction. ... ### NEG-8 ... A supposedly minimal representation loses provenance or temporal distinctions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Pre-registers eight candidate negative results to actively search for (NEG-1..8): a fourth value C cannot distinguish contradiction subtypes; structured evaluation still collapses required distinctions; contradiction is context-dependent and cannot be represented without context; contradiction is temporal and cannot be represented statically; source conflict is not epistemic contradiction; contradiction cannot be reduced to Sat; Zero cannot be determined from contradiction alone; a supposedly minimal representation loses provenance or temporal distinctions.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
### Candidate I1 ... $$
Contr(p,K)\not\equiv Unknown(p,K)
$$ ... ### Candidate I10 ... Historical contradiction and current contradiction may differ.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Fourth attack — retraction ... E_1 is later invalidated. Retract(E_1). We cannot simply delete E_1. We must find Dependents(E_1). Then recompute affected assertions. This gives us Retraction \rightarrow DependencyAnalysis \rightarrow KnowledgeRevision.

b_rows_sample.statement: Designs the fifth adversarial test (partial requirement satisfaction), showing Sufficient(K_t,C_G)=False evaluates only against the explicit contract, not universal knowledge.

a_rows_sample.statement: The kernel lane's single output, Claim Strength <= Evidence Strength, is identified as this research programme's own standing governing rule ('the strongest statement made must never exceed the strength of the available evidence'), independently reached via the Gita Ch16 lens -- assessed as the strongest convergence in the entire Gita track, not for philosophical depth but because the programme has been executing this rule for four days and can point to its own corrections (REFUTED->NOT ESTABLISHED, closed->classification closed, forced->repair class forced) as evidence it is operable. This matters because Step 291 sec07 ruled 'do not call an engineering TODO a governance decision' -- the converse risk here is that part of Qualify is normative and thus resolvable by authority, yet has been sitting in the irreducible pile. b_rows_sample.anchor: False \neq Unknown \neq Unqualified
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three epistemic outcomes that must not be conflated: False (evidence contradicts p, p->R); Unknown (insufficient evidence, p->Z, i.e. Zero); Unqualified (evidence exists but the system cannot yet establish it satisfies required criteria, p->Q). Zero given a precise role: B(x)=G means 'insufficient knowledge to determine this' distinct from B(x)=R ('rejected') and B(x)=U ('evidence does not determine the result'). Proposed as potentially fundamental to the KnowledgeOS epistemic kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify(x)\rightarrow \{Qualified,\ Unqualified,\ Undetermined,\ Terminus\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines Qualify beyond a binary Qualified=True/False into Qualify(x)->{Qualified, Unqualified, Undetermined, Terminus}, connecting to the Cavell insight (justification may legitimately terminate). Qualify != prove everything; Qualify = determine whether the available basis is sufficient for the intended epistemic act; the correct result is sometimes Terminus rather than another investigation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim Strength \leq Evidence Strength
b_rows_sample.statement: From the divine-vs-destructive qualities discussion, proposes an 'epistemic restraint' operator: the kernel must ask not only 'what can I conclude' but 'what am I permitted to conclude from what I have', giving the candidate invariant Claim Strength <= Evidence Strength -- e.g. E(x)=weak must not produce C(x)=certain without an additional legitimate transformation. Proposed as a powerful candidate KnowledgeOS assurance rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge growth ... Knowledge expansion ... Knowledge purification ... These are not equivalent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects Purification=increase-in-dimensions-and-values as the canonical mathematical definition (confidence 0.95->0.55 can represent improvement if the original confidence was unjustified): Purification != monotonic increase; P(K_t,K_{t+1}) = improvement in epistemic quality, with quality itself still needing formal definition. Distinguishes three non-equivalent concepts: Knowledge growth (K_t->K_{t+1}, a state change occurs); Knowledge expansion (dim(K_{t+1})>dim(K_t), new dimensions represented); Knowledge purification (P(K_t,K_{t+1})=true, epistemic quality improves) -- more information does not imply better knowledge, and knowledge expansion != knowledge purification, assessed as an important theoretical safeguard. Also reformulates purification against Sigma as Sigma_t --B,Q,delta--> Sigma_{t+1} with P(Sigma_t,Sigma_{t+1}) rather than a scalar purity score, given Step 287's problem with total ordering.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Accepted(K) \cap Rejected(K) = \varnothing ... Unknown(K)\not\equiv Rejected(K) ... Unqualified(K)\not\equiv Unknown(K)

Also gives four-way kernel decomposition: kernel primitives {Represent, Discriminate, Qualify, DetectGap, Transform}; kernel state K_t; kernel control properties {Restraint, Consistency, Provenance, Uncertainty}; external governance {Authority, Policy, Authorization, Action} -- explicitly warning that Authority must not be placed inside Buddhi merely because Buddhi can determine what appears right, preserving the Steps 285-287 architecture.

a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that Chapter 15's kernel-identity invariant (M != K_t; Identity(M_t)=Identity(M_{t+1}) while K_t!=K_{t+1} is permitted; 'persistent kernel identity + mutable epistemic state') is 25I.30 (KnowledgeIdentity is persistent; KnowledgeState evolves) and 258.2 (Identity persistence != value equality) restated one level up, from the assertion level to the kernel level. At the assertion level, a later construction (id=H(P,e,c,t,Pi) with mutable e.state, executed per 288/06 sec H) VIOLATED this invariant; at the kernel level nothing has been built yet, so stating it now is cheap (proposed prospectively before any construction can violate it). Still marked [H] (hypothesis) because it presupposes kernel identity, and Step 291 records operation identity OPEN at 0 of 22 -- a kernel has no identity rule either, so the invariant is well-formed but has no subject.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Type-correct composition over four undefined carriers and one defined one. Well-formed. Uninstantiable. A THIRD T4-SHAPE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Audits every carrier in the type-correct tau o delta o Z composition: G_t (gap/zero state) has no carrier anywhere (Z is O-vocabulary item #6 per G-91); E_t (evidence) blocked since Qualify is G1 (evidence has no admission procedure); C_t (context) untyped per gap G-15; D_t (decision) is now a FIFTH rival decision codomain (joining 25S.3, 38.10, 012 sec35, 012 sec36); only Sigma_t is a defined carrier (5 axes, 2240 states, corpus-verified). Classifies M=(S,O,o,delta,tau,I) as the third T4-SHAPE on record (after 20's K=(K_t,Omega_K,I), all 3 slots empty, and 22's 5-slot operation-identity schema, all slots empty) with 4 of 5 carriers undefined -- the most complete of the three (the only one that type-checks) but still a shape; Step 291's Audit H rule (shape->content needs a derivation) applies unchanged.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a symbol collision ... this lane assigns the corpus's `δ` role to `τ`.
a_rows_sample.statement: New gap G-95: a delta glyph collision. This lane's delta:(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t denotes discrimination and returns a decision, while the corpus's delta(K,o)->K' denotes the transition function and returns a state; different codomains, same glyph, and this lane actually assigns the corpus's delta role to its own tau instead. Marked as the third glyph collision on record (after O operations-vs-observations, and cong/equiv overloading), documentary. New gap G-96: Qualify now carries three roles across the corpus -- the G1 function, an operator Q in this lane's operator vocabulary, and (here) a decision outcome value in d in {Accept,Reject,Uncertain,Contradictory,Investigate,Qualify} -- a third role for that name, documentary plus formal. Registers ninth negative constraint C9: M != K_t (the kernel must not become identical to the state it produces).

b_rows_sample.anchor: All FOUR junctions are ill-typed. The composition is not merely unproven — it does not typecheck anywhere.
b_rows_sample.statement: Precisely diagnoses why Theta_total fails: the five operators are Theta_A:A_t->A_{t+1} (carrier N, the knower), Theta_T:T->T_detached (carrier T, transformations themselves), Theta_K:K_t->K_{t+1} (carrier K), Theta_I:A_t->K_atma (carrier N->K_atma, a different codomain), Theta_X:X_t->X_{t+1} (carrier W, the world). The claimed composition Theta_total = Theta_X o Theta_I o Theta_K o Theta_T o Theta_A requires codomain(f)=domain(g) at four junctions, all ill-typed: Theta_A->Theta_T needs N=T (knower vs transformations); Theta_T->Theta_K needs T=K (transformations vs states); Theta_K->Theta_I needs K=N, but N notin K is ratified (FA-4[E]), so this junction contradicts the lane's own strongest shared finding; Theta_I->Theta_X needs K_atma=W (an identity vs the world). Register upgrade: Theta_total moves from 'RX -- type-check failure across four carriers' to 'RX -- all four composition junctions ill-typed, one against a ratified result' -- a sharper statement of the same verdict, not a new one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two ORTHOGONAL classifications of \mathcal O. Crossing them gives a 2-D grid.
b_rows_sample.statement: Discarding the ill-typed composition but keeping the classification: the five Theta operators constitute a CARRIER taxonomy (what an operation acts on: N knower, T transformations, K state, identity, W world), orthogonal to Step 259.7's FUNCTIONAL taxonomy (what an operation does: state-transformations, assessments, governance, audit/history, observation). Since Step 291 established the missing piece is a mandatory-membership rule (not an enumeration), and a rule on one axis cannot see distinctions on the other, this sharpens gap N-4: the membership rule needs two indices. Example cells: Withdraw (functional: state-transformation, carrier: K, currently in registry); Authorize (functional: governance, carrier: unstated -- acts on N or W?); TraceOrigin (functional: observation, carrier: provenance, unregistered per 291 sec02); Theta_T-like (no functional class fits, carrier T, not in any registry). Explicitly: this sharpens N-4, it does not solve it; no membership is proposed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is \mathcal O closed under operations that take operations as arguments? The corpus has never asked.
b_rows_sample.statement: New gap G-93: Theta_T:T->T_detached is a transformation of a transformation (higher-order); nothing in Step 259.7's five functional kinds, the 22-operation registry, or Step 291's nine closure senses is higher-order, so the corpus has never asked whether O is closed under higher-order operations. But the corpus already contains a live instance unrecognised as such: Vairagya/Karma-phala-tyaga is T->T_detached, recorded as R6 via invariant I-V ('no Admissible conjunct reads the outcome'); I-V is a constraint ON a transformation, i.e. a higher-order predicate -- so the corpus already reasons about T at second order without having declared O admits it. This is not a philosophical import; the corpus's own I-V forces the question. The operation-membership rule N-4 must decide whether O contains higher-order operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Three independent sources converge on a ~5-slot decomposition of an operation
b_rows_sample.statement: Discards Ch18's (18.13-18) five-factor action mapping (Divine->K_atma is RX; Body->K_t misreads the state as an instrument) but keeps the arity and slot roles, finding a three-source convergence on a ~5-slot operation decomposition: Ch18 (instrument, doer, means/senses, endeavour, enabling source); H-290-1/Ch5 (intended act, acting subject, instruments, context, resulting transformation); and Step 259.7's own signature Authorize:Actor x Action x Policy -> Decision, which already contains 'doer' and 'enabling condition' slots. Two of the five slots are already present in an existing corpus signature -- assessed as completing a pattern the corpus started, not an import. Gives operation identity a SHAPE (id(o) over doer/instrument/means/endeavour/enabling-condition), addressing Step 291's finding that operation identity is OPEN (0 of 22), but not a RULE: which slots are identity-bearing is exactly Step 258.20's question (OperationalIdentity(x) iff exists T in T: changing id(x) changes T(K,c)), which quantifies over the unenumerated T, the same blocker. Registered O-Q1: T4-SHAPE, correctly shaped but unpopulated, like K=(K_t,Omega_K,I) in artifact 20; not promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZERO gaps discharged. TWO sharpened, ONE shaped. That is the honest yield, and it is not nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Updated gap-register optimization: of N-4 (membership), operation identity, equiv (minimal cut), Qualify (G1), delta (commit case), the metric (M-Q3prime), (Omega,F,P) (G-22), and canonical K -- none is discharged; N-4 and operation identity are sharpened/shaped; the rest unchanged or worsened by inspection (e.g. K_supreme=sup(Omega) presupposes a nonexistent order per artifact 19's E1; K=f(F,A_t) already refused per artifact 18). Confirms artifact 18's finding from the opposite direction: the Gita is rich in distinctions and empty of carriers; every gap in the register is a membership/procedure/carrier question, while every contribution this lane makes is a distinction -- distinctions sharpen questions, only carriers close them. Explicitly did not edit/correct/supersede any external_research artifact (a registry act per artifact 19), did not propose O-Q1/O-Q2 as architecture, and confirms Steps 288-291 remain unchanged, all R6.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the type-checking lane produced the usable result — and it is the one that claims less.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive contrast with artifact 22: the external_research Theta_total (5 operators) has 4 of 4 junctions ill-typed and flattens Sigma to 3 modes while self-declaring 'Complete'; this lane's composition (3 operators: Z:K_t->G_t, delta:(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t, tau:(K_t,D_t)->K_{t+1}, i.e. tau o delta o Z) has 0 of its junctions ill-typed, respects the ratified 5-axis Sigma, and self-declares 'must not yet be declared canonical'. Same source material, opposite discipline; the type-checking lane produced the usable result and is the one that claims less. Explicitly flags that type-correct is not the same as instantiable (developed further in sec5).

a_rows_sample.statement: Concrete worked example testing the accumulated kernel model: kernel receives assertion 'the production deployment has succeeded' with no runtime evidence (E=empty-set); runs Observe->Discriminate->Qualify(P,E,C,T,Pi); Zero detects Z(K_t)=missing evidence; the kernel does NOT conclude P=false, reconfirming Unknown != False as one of the strongest results of the Gita+Zero interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: o_t = \Omega_{G_t} \left( B_t,K_t,Z_t \right)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the guna mode as selecting an operator POLICY, not merely a descriptive label: o_t = Omega_{G_t}(B_t,K_t,Z_t), giving Tamas mode o=Ignore; Rajas mode o=Search->Act->Search; Sattva mode o=Discriminate->Qualify->(Act or Stop) -- illustrated on identical K_t and O_t across modes, giving 'different modes of mind -> different operators/behaviour' a formal shape.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \operatorname{Stop}(K_t) ... No further qualification is presently justified.
a_rows_sample.statement: Discovers a missing operator through simulation: when Buddhi cannot determine sufficiency, the kernel needs Escalate or SeekQualification -- the kernel must know when NOT to decide. Proposes Stop(K_t) as a legitimate kernel operation: a disciplined kernel can say 'no further qualification is presently justified', which is an epistemic decision, not a failure -- contrasted with a bad kernel's uncertainty->more computation->more computation loop. Gives Qualify(x) codomain {Qualified,Rejected,Suspended,Escalated,bot}, with bot meaning the kernel has reached a legitimate epistemic terminus, connecting to the Cavell insight.

a_rows_sample.anchor: J_t = w_A A_t+ w_S S_t+ w_R R_t+ w_V V_t+ w_C C_t - \lambda Z_t - \mu U_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes, explicitly non-canonical/for research purposes only, a candidate kernel objective function J_t = w_A A_t + w_S S_t + w_R R_t + w_V V_t + w_C C_t - lambda Z_t - mu U_t (weighted five Sigma axes minus unresolved-gap term Z minus unjustified-commitment term U), with purification meaning J_{t+1}>J_t -- explicitly not adopted because the measurement scales and per-axis ordering remain unresolved (per Step 287). Proposes Moksha as the limiting condition where repeated purification cycles reach Delta J -> 0 (the kernel can no longer improve the state under the available epistemic horizon) -- a philosophical hypothesis, not an architecture decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P1 — Kernel is active ... P7 — Kernel mode affects operation selection
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven candidate principles from the simulation: P1 Kernel != Knowledge Store (active epistemic processor); P2 Buddhi=discrimination, B:state+observation+context->epistemic discrimination; P3 Knowledge is dynamic, K_t!=K_{t+1}; P4 Zero is epistemically constructive, Zero(K_t)=representation of detected absence/obstruction; P5 Purification is quality transformation, Purify(K_t) not-equiv AddKnowledge(K_t); P6 Outcome is independent from epistemic validity, valid reasoning != successful outcome; P7 Kernel mode affects operation selection, G_t -> Omega_{G_t} -- assessed as the potential mathematical foundation for the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest persistent epistemic mechanism capable of representing a knowledge state, discriminating over it, and producing a governed transformation of that state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes the smallest meaningful kernel cannot be merely a data structure; needs at least Represent + Discriminate + Transform, with Zero/Purification/Action/Guna/provenance understood around this core. Candidate research definition (explicitly not ratified canonical): KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest persistent epistemic mechanism capable of representing a knowledge state, discriminating over it, and producing a governed transformation of that state -- explicitly noting Steps 285-287 deliberately leave canonicalization, equality, Qualify, and governance unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: input \rightarrow precondition \rightarrow Buddhi decision \rightarrow state transformation \rightarrow postcondition \rightarrow Zero effect \rightarrow provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the concluding research step 'Define the Kernel Algebra': stop adding Gita chapters and take the simulated kernel through a formal operator analysis of {Observe,Attend,Discriminate,Qualify,Compare,Transform,Purify,Act,Expose,Stabilize,Stop,Escalate}, determining for every operator a 7-step profile: input -> precondition -> Buddhi decision -> state transformation -> postcondition -> Zero effect -> provenance, then testing composition, idempotence, commutativity, associativity, reversibility, monotonicity, mode-dependence and purification effects -- framed as turning the philosophical interpretation into an actual mathematical research programme.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 11 fenced blocks. ALL are ```text. ZERO are code. ... it does NOT overclaim
a_rows_sample.statement: Audits S2252's kernel 'simulation' as a sixth artifact carrying a title (simulation/executable) the programme has previously found (INV-9/EV-F2) to contain no program in five prior corpus steps; this one likewise contains zero executable code (11 fenced blocks, all plain text). Unlike those five, this artifact does NOT overclaim empirical validation -- its own opening states it is a hypothetical test of internal coherence, not a claim the Gita defines KnowledgeOS. Classified as evidence class ANALYTIC-worked-scenario, not EXECUTED, correctly scoped by its own text and must never be cited as executed evidence -- recorded because the word 'simulation' in the title risks being misread as execution by a later agent who sees only the title.

a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a simulation model (K_t,Sigma_t,G_t) --Buddhi+O_i--> (K_{t+1},Sigma_{t+1},G_{t+1}), with a trajectory K_0-O1->K_1-O2->K_2->...->K_n measured against the discovered invariants via Sigma_0,...,Sigma_n -- 'purification becomes something we can simulate rather than merely describe.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Operation execution \neq operation authorship
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.27's 'I am the doer' bewilderment (activities actually carried out through the modes of nature, not imported theologically): proposes Operation execution != operation authorship, decomposing Operation into intent, actor, mechanism, context, authorization, execution, result -- assessed as precisely the separation the existing provenance/authority model needs. Also, from 5.8-9's five causes of action (doer, work, situation, endeavor, fortune, not promoted as five primitives), proposes the analytical decomposition Action=f(Actor,Operation,Context,Effort,Contingency), reinforcing the principle 'do not collapse operation, actor, context, authority and outcome into one object'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Operation validity \neq desired outcome
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.10-12 (relinquishing attachment to fruit): Operation validity != desired outcome -- 'the system must evaluate whether an operation was epistemically/technically justified independently of whether it produced the desired result'. Worked example: Hypothesis->Qualification->Action->Outcome=failure does not automatically mean Qualification=invalid; conversely Outcome=success does not prove Qualification=valid -- assessed as a profound connection to deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the interfaces through which information/action crosses the kernel boundary
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.13's city of nine gates (the self not identifying with the body's activities): proposes a kernel boundary concept distinguishing internal reasoning (state/Buddhi/qualification/transformation) from external interfaces (input/output, observation/action) -- 'the gates' understood as interfaces through which information/action crosses the kernel boundary, treated strictly as a philosophical model, not literal architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should not claim that Chapter 5 solves semantic equality ... it does not provide the decision procedure for K_1\equiv K_2
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.18's equal vision (wise person sees equally despite differences in external form): proposes NormalizePerspective(x) -- distinguish superficial representation from underlying epistemic identity, normalizing different representations before comparing underlying semantics. Explicitly and critically caveats: the Gita provides a philosophical hypothesis for why deeper equivalence matters, but does NOT provide the decision procedure for K_1 equiv K_2 (the Step 287 equality problem remains unsolved).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel invariant: discrimination should remain stable under perturbation ... d(K,x,c) \approx d(K',x,c')
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.20's sthira-buddhi (steady, unbewildered intelligence): proposes the kernel invariant that discrimination should remain stable under perturbation. Formalizes Buddhi(K,x,c)->d and proposes stability means d(K,x,c) approx d(K',x,c') under changes that are not decision-relevant -- explicitly connected to (but not identical with) the provenance/equality work. From 5.23/5.27-28, models desire, fear and anger (not literalized as human emotion) as biasing perturbations: constructs B(K,x) as a bias/perturbation function that Buddhi must discriminate from signal -- highly relevant to AI systems.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q(K_{t+1}) > Q(K_t) ... 100 pieces of noisy knowledge \downarrow purification \downarrow 20 pieces of highly qualified knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: From 5.11 (purification through disciplined action without attachment): sharpens purification from |K_{t+1}|>|K_t| to Q(K_{t+1})>Q(K_t) where Q is a future epistemic-quality function. Concrete illustration: a kernel could transform 100 pieces of noisy knowledge into 20 pieces of highly qualified knowledge, becoming better despite becoming smaller -- assessed as a major correction to a purely information-quantity model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Kernel State ... A kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit separation: Knowledge State K_t answers 'what does the system currently represent/know', Kernel State (fraktur K)_t = (K_t,M_t,B_t,Z_t,Pi_t) answers 'in what condition is the system currently processing that knowledge'. K_t != (fraktur K)_t: a kernel can contain excellent knowledge while operating in a poor mode, or hold incomplete knowledge with excellent discrimination/qualification behaviour -- assessed as very important for the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model. Candidate kernel transition: (fraktur K)_t --Buddhi--> o_t --Purify--> (fraktur K)_{t+1}. Final consolidated formula: K_{t+1}=Purify(Execute(Buddhi(K_t,O_t,C_t))). Concluding principle: the Kernel is not the Knowledge; the Kernel is the smallest active unit that operates on Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.statement: Section 4.1-4.2: under the widened 66-world design (full product over the 5 perturbable rows x 2 edge variants, versus the original 14-world design), the closure-size range widens from 15..22 to 15..23 -- meaning the prior negative claim ('the kernel requirement set's size is not determined by the corpus') actually understated itself; the 5-item triply-robust blocked set {Identity, InvariantReg, K, Proposition, Relation} is unchanged even at 4.7x the world count, named the strongest positive result in the package, with InvariantReg (the un-enumerated invariant register, G-67) confirmed as blocked under literally every tested reading of every axis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: And 'blocked in 66 of 66 worlds' is not evidence of absence ... exec/extend_k9_worlds.py:15 hard-codes the premise: G_str['InvariantReg'] = (['K'], 'NOT ENUMERATED', 'D') ... 66/66 therefore measures the robustness of the closure computation to world choice — it does not measure the enumeration status of ℐ. ... the premise is the claim it is offered to support.
b_rows_sample.statement: Critically re-examines the widely-cited '66 of 66 worlds' robustness finding (from a prior batch's k9-closure computation) supporting the InvariantReg-never-enumerated premise: finds the source code exec/extend_k9_worlds.py line 15 HARD-CODES the string 'NOT ENUMERATED' as an INPUT to all 66 world variants, so the 66/66 result measures only the robustness of the closure computation to world CHOICE, not the actual enumeration status of the invariant register -- the computation itself is sound, but its premise is exactly the claim it was being offered as evidence FOR. a_rows_sample.anchor: Avacchedaka -- Ruling: both -- the principle is universal; the device is a modelling technique.
a_rows_sample.statement: Special Area A ruling: a claim without its delimiting conditions over-applies (the bounded-context violation, DDD 'same data shape != same concept') -- this corruption is not domain-specific, it is the definition of meaning-loss, so the principle is Universal; the formal delimiting-conditions tuple (Entity.Property.Context.Relation.Time.Authority) is a REPRESENTATION technique, one way among several to express the boundary, not itself a kernel law. Consequence: the principle enters the Adopted Core (law 1); the tuple is deferred to REPRESENTATION.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = Neutral starting condition ... It begins as: UNKNOWN
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero as neutral knowledge state: Zero != Nothing, it is a neutral starting condition. A new knowledge object begins without authority, evidence, validation or interpretation -- it begins as UNKNOWN.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: UNKNOWN is proposed as a first-class state, distinct from False and from Missing: UNKNOWN = a known, unresolved state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: UNKNOWN != False. UNKNOWN != Missing. UNKNOWN = Known unresolved state
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero lens: UNKNOWN restated as a first-class known-unresolved state, distinct from False and Missing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not force: Unknown -> False / Unknown -> Guess / Unknown -> Empty. Instead: Unknown -> Known Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Combining Zero ('unknown is a valid state') with ECS ('failure does not destroy truth, failure pauses advancement'): Unknown should be preserved and later resolved, never forced into False/Guess/Empty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the elephant-and-blind-men story (cited by the source) not as 'everyone is equally right' but as 'different observations may represent different projections of the same underlying object', formalized as perspectives A/B/C/D undergoing structural comparison to yield a common invariant = ZERO.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Abstracts the source's citation of Subhash Kak's six-darsanas-as-cube-walls metaphor into the principle 'knowledge is perspective dependent, but structure may be perspective invariant', with the research question 'what survives when we rotate the perspective?' answered by ZERO = invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds ... The technology disappears. The invariant remains.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces modal Zero Z_M(K) = invariant across plausible worlds, alongside a claimed prior representation Zero Z_R(K)=invariant across representations and temporal Zero Z_T(K)=invariant across time; illustrated by four possible event-bus technology choices (Kafka/RabbitMQ/sync API/another event bus) all preserving the invariant requirement 'evidence publication must remain replayable' -- the technology disappears, the invariant remains.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = ⋂_i Structure(I_i) ... What structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times, and perspectives? That may be one of our strongest candidates for robust knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the Zero lens as Z=intersection_i Structure(I_i) over interpretations generated from multiple world models W1..Wn (not necessarily literal set intersection in implementation), asking what structure remains invariant across competing models, representations, times and perspectives, proposed as one of the strongest candidates for robust knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_i = π_i(R) ... O1 ≠ O2 doesn't necessarily mean R1 ≠ R2. It may simply mean π1 ≠ π2. This gives us a very useful projection lens.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the elephant analogy as a projection: observation Oi=pi_i(R) for underlying reality/object R and observer perspective pi_i, concluding that differing observations O1!=O2 need not imply differing underlying realities R1!=R2 -- it may simply reflect differing perspectives pi1!=pi2 -- named the 'projection lens'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z = Invariant(O1,...,On) ... Zero is not "nothing." It is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Given observations O1..On, defines Z=Invariant(O1,...,On) and explicitly corrects a possible misreading: Zero is not 'nothing', it is the minimum invariant structure that survives changes in representation -- called one of the strongest concepts in the entire exploration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dhātu = transformation structure ... Zero = invariant structure ... what changed? / what remained?
b_rows_sample.statement: States a Dhatu/Zero duality: given O1 --T1--> O2 --T2--> O3, Dhatu asks what transformation generated the new state (Dhatu = transformation structure) while Zero asks what remained (Zero = invariant structure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens result on Williamson: after removing beliefs, documents, language, databases, probabilities, possible worlds, embeddings, topics, LLMs, what survives is minimal: 'A participant is related to a proposition/content in a world/context/time such that the proposition is true and the participant is in a factive state of knowing.' Knowledge itself should not be reduced to its representations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Participants make commitments. 2. Commitments have inferential consequences. 3. Some commitments are supported/entitled...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brandom (removing language/English/sentences/speech/Frege/Wittgenstein/philosophy) yields ten survivor claims: participants make commitments; commitments have inferential consequences; some commitments are supported/entitled; commitments can conflict; participants assess one another's commitments; new actions alter the state; implicit relations can become explicit; concepts are characterized partly by inferential roles; objectivity can emerge within social assessment; a claim is not merely a string but a position in a normative/inferential structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is not simply an error state. It is a legitimate epistemic condition.
b_rows_sample.statement: ASP answer-set semantics give TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN query results and ground at least three distinct kinds of 'unknown': unknown because alternatives remain (P and ¬P both possible), unknown because the agent is unaware (neither represented), and unknown because a default was blocked (an exception/missing condition prevented an otherwise-applicable default). The earlier flat UNKNOWN category should become an Epistemic Status taxonomy: true/false/unresolved-alternatives/not-represented-unaware/defeasibly-inferable-but-blocked/etc; the exact taxonomy remains a research question but the distinction itself is now strongly grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence must not silently become an epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Danger flagged in the Projection model: 'If Projection P2 doesn't contain X, therefore X is false' would be wrong, since absence from a projection could mean not relevant, not visible, not assessed, outside scope, unavailable, superseded, or genuinely no longer justified — these are different meanings. This connects to the ZERO lens: absence must not silently become an epistemic state, giving another reason to preserve ZERO discipline within the Projection idea.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(e) ∈ {alternative, unrepresented, blocked-default, outside-scope, computationally-unresolved}
b_rows_sample.statement: Unknownness U(e) is proposed not as a Boolean but a classification (alternative / unrepresented / blocked-default / outside-scope / computationally-unresolved), with the exact taxonomy left empirical and countable for future statistical analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. There is an underlying world/domain. 2. A participant has beliefs/knowledge about it. 3. Only part of that knowledge may be explicitly represented...
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens extraction on Brachman & Levesque (removing FOL/Prolog/frames/description logic/SAT/default logic/Bayesian networks/STRIPS/GOLOG) yields twelve survivor claims: an underlying world/domain exists; a participant has beliefs/knowledge about it; only part is explicitly represented; representation is a mapping between domains; reasoning derives implicit content from explicit content; meaning depends on interpretation/context; different representation languages have different expressive power; reasoning capability is resource-limited; knowledge changes and can be revised; uncertainty/vagueness require richer representations; the same knowledge may have different representations; action depends on knowledge — described as extraordinarily close to the current model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: what survives across *both* phases is: **a knower/participant · something known · a ground · and a record that the two were connected.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero-Lens applied across both phases: after stripping optional attributes, what survives universally is a knower/participant, something known, a ground, and a record that the two were connected — every phase and nearly every model retains those four; nothing else survives universally. The corpus distinguishes 'nothing exists' from 'we do not know' (0258: 'Knowledge is not only about what exists'; formal law §9: unknown≠absent≠false). Whether UNKNOWN is the absence of Knowledge or a state of an identified object is NOT resolved by the corpus: formal law (⟨Z-1⟩) says UNKNOWN/ABSENT/FALSE/REJECTED are states of an identified epistemic object, while kernel document 125708 §17 pushes the other way ('UNKNOWN must not be a single epistemic state', eight readings) — no new state proposed here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AF-004 · Zero's chronology inverts CF-005's apparent ordering
b_rows_sample.statement: The repository's 'third sense' of Zero (Z-KOS-001 meta-principle) and the absence-lens sense are BOTH dated 2026-08-22; the goal-gap function sense is the LATEST (2026-08-27 era) — inverting an apparent ordering implied by CF-005.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-005 · Zero naming collision — a third sense
b_rows_sample.statement: Repository Zero (Z-KOS-001) is a foundational meta-principle explicitly refused as kernel article and implementation object ('Zero is the name for that prevention', 'Zero != Component = Property of the boundaries'), whereas v0.2 Zero is the computable goal-gap function Zero(K, EC); same term, incompatible senses, extending the CON-01 lineage with an implementation-side third sense; no repository counterpart of the goal-gap function exists, and the eta-totality/G-residual question (T-9) stays open.

a_aliases: UNKNOWN is a valid epistemic state
