b_aliases: Searle Construction of Social Reality lens

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit preservation note keeping every named technology recommendation level-tagged as a hypothesis, never promoted to adopted architecture, while noting the existing PHP/Laravel + TypeScript/Vue platform is the ESTABLISHED current stack.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DI principle vs framework import: adopt the DI/composition-root principle without adopting Spring — the corpus wants the first, but the kernel file pairs the principle with the Spring runtime.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
a_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
a_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule 1 -- No new research concepts ... Rule 2 -- Preserve identity discipline ... Rule 3 -- Separate the three layers
b_rows_sample.statement: Three Mandatory Discipline Rules for P4: (1) No new research concepts -- anything not already extracted is marked Candidate, never admitted as established; the map consolidates, it does not collect. (2) Preserve identity discipline -- Similarity != Identity; every invariant is validated by its ID, evidence lineage, original registration, and validation state; no look-alike row is accepted on resemblance. (3) Separate the three layers -- Kernel Invariant (constitutional, PRESERVE), Reasoning Mechanism (operational, GOVERN -- engines: LLM, TMS, AGM, logic solver), Representation (Vani/expression layer); a row must not blur its layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Similarity =/= Identity ... Do not merge concepts because they sound similar. Validate using: ID, Evidence lineage, Original registration, Validation state
b_rows_sample.statement: Rule 2 (full form, the origin statement of the identity discipline later applied throughout P4/P5): apply the Navya-Nyaya-derived principle Similarity != Identity; do not merge concepts because they sound similar; validate every concept using ID, evidence lineage, original registration, and validation state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Wrong: KnowledgeOS uses graphs -> kernel invariant. Correct: Relationship preservation -> constitutional concern; Graph database -> implementation option
b_rows_sample.statement: Rule 3 (full form) with a worked wrong/correct example: every extracted concept must belong to exactly one of three layers -- Layer 1 Constitutional Kernel Invariant, Layer 2 Reasoning/Epistemic Mechanism, Layer 3 Representation/Implementation Concern. Wrong: 'KnowledgeOS uses graphs -> kernel invariant.' Correct: 'Relationship preservation -> constitutional concern; Graph database -> implementation option.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel ... Reasoning Engines ... They operate inside kernel constraints
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 4: the Kernel is responsible for identity preservation, provenance, epistemic boundaries, validity rules, transformation integrity. Reasoning Engines (LLM reasoning, theorem provers, TMS, AGM revision, Bayesian models, human reasoning) operate inside kernel constraints.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT implement mathematics. Only classify usefulness.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 5 template table (Mathematics | Contribution | Kernel Status): Topology - invariants across transformation - Lens; Type Theory - identity preservation - Lens; Lattice Theory - ordering/revision - Candidate mechanism; Temporal Logic - validity over time - Lens; Category Theory - composition - Research lens. Instruction: do not implement mathematics, only classify its usefulness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is Constitutional Rules ... it does not do the reasoning. Reasoning Engines are Operational Mechanisms
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 4 (binding, SS16): the Kernel defines what is legally permissible in knowledge evolution, prevents dimension collapse, preserves identity/evidence/knower, but does not do the reasoning; Reasoning Engines execute reasoning/hypothesis-generation/revision within the constitutional constraints -- 'the kernel provides the inviolable playing field where reasoning can happen safely without corrupting the epistemic record.' Three layers with verbs: Kernel Invariant/PRESERVE (all 29 rows), Reasoning Mechanism/GOVERN (LLM, TMS, AGM, Logic Solver, Simulation, Human Expert, the Validation Layer, Intent-001's engine-side), Representation/ENABLE (Vani/expression, type model, epistemic graph/hypergraph, record-shapes). Boundary rule: 'AI reasons. KnowledgeOS governs reasoning.' Fallibilism applies to the kernel itself (SS17): the kernel is sealed against corruption, not against revision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematics should describe, not define.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 5, Mathematical Lens Consolidation: type model (Claim<T>, K1.extension==K2.extension does not imply K1==K2) consolidates into Context-002 + INV-KOS-002 + Representation!=Identity (Representation layer); topological/relational representation consolidates into Relationship-001 + Relation-001 + Context-002 (Representation layer); epistemic graph/hypergraph consolidates into Relation-001 + Reasoning-Provenance-001 + Context-002 (3x reproduced conclusion, Representation layer); logic (Vyapti, hetvabhasa-as-type-failures, temporal logic) consolidates into Vyapti-001 + Inference-001 + Fallacy-001/Failure-001 (Kernel-as-lens); temporal (valid-from/valid-until/expired/state-as-fold/forward-only) consolidates into the Temporal family + Revisability-001 (Kernel). 'The lenses are descriptions of already-registered content, never new content themselves.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Article I.1 ... Article I.2 ... Article I.3 -- Mathematics describes, never defines.
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter I, the Constitutional Identity: Article I.1 the character (KnowledgeOS governs how knowledge is created/justified/transformed/challenged/evolved while preserving identity/context/evidence/authority/reasoning/uncertainty/agency/historical evolution); Article I.2 the three clause refinements (existence, reasoning, identity) are constitutionally absorbed as phrasing refinements, not supersessions; Article I.3 the governing maxim 'Mathematics describes, never defines' -- topology, type theory, graphs, TMS, AGM, LLMs are mechanisms/explanatory lenses, never kernel law by virtue of being mathematical or computational.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONSTITUTIONAL KERNEL <- the eleven articles (PRESERVE) ... Engine Layer (GOVERN) ... Mechanisms (GOVERN) ... Representations (ENABLE) ... Implementation (ENABLE)
b_rows_sample.statement: Chapter III, the Kernel Boundary: a 5-tier diagram -- Constitutional Kernel (the 11 articles, PRESERVE) served by Engine Layer (validation engines, fallacy detection, debate pipeline, intent classification, verdict vocabulary, GOVERN), Mechanisms (epistemic-inquiry lifecycle, reasoning pipelines, GOVERN), Representations (evidence records, context tuples, epistemic state model, absence taxonomy, epistemic graph, typed encodings, ENABLE), and Implementation (storage, interfaces, systems, deliberately unconstrained, ENABLE). III.1 the kernel does not do the reasoning -- it states what must be preserved/never collapse; engines execute governed transformations realizing those constraints. III.2 no engine/mechanism/representation may violate an article -- evolution that violates an article is a corruption, not an evolution, subject to Chapter V. III.3 implementation is deliberately out of constitutional scope.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel != KnowledgeOS Primitive ... Kernel = computational boundary operating on Knowledge State. This is a much cleaner DDD interpretation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Resolves a Step 285 confusion: the Kernel should operate over the eight ratified primitives {Entity,State,Event,Observation,Proposition,Relation,Policy,Action} but is not itself another primitive -- KnowledgeOS Kernel != KnowledgeOS Primitive; rather Kernel = computational boundary operating on Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The eight primitives describe what exists in the kernel state. They do not yet completely describe what the kernel does. ... Kernel State != Kernel Algebra ... we still need to determine the operators Omega = {operators of the kernel}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Draws the distinction Kernel State != Kernel Algebra: the eight primitives describe what exists in the kernel state but not what the kernel does; the operator set Omega = {operators of the kernel} still needs to be determined, with Buddhi as the candidate central philosophical model for that operator layer.

group_evidence.why_grouped: an UNKNOWN-OBJECT-CANDIDATE row (batch B0050, source S2048) named these as alternative candidates for one piece of evidence. why_uncertain: unclear whether this 10-tuple state/6-stage-transition proposal is meant as, or corresponds to, the pre-existing 'kos-kernel-engine-boundary' or 'knowledgeos-kernel-concept' objects, since several of its components (Σ_t, H_t, G_t, C_t) are used without definition or cross-reference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion contains a proposition. That does not mean P subset A. ... Containment \neq Set Inclusion ... P \xrightarrow{embedded in} A \xrightarrow{member of} K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the K_P subset K_A subset K_J subset K_t subset Omega chain as a category error: propositions, assertions and knowledge states are different types of object, and containment (a proposition being embedded in an assertion) is not the same relation as set inclusion (an assertion being a member of a knowledge state's assertion set); replaces it with a typed composition chain (embedded-in / member-of / subset-of).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Instead of A=(P,Sigma,E,tau,Pi), use Supports(E,A) or EvidenceRelation(E,A,r) where r in {supports,contradicts,qualifies,weakens,contextualizes}
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes moving Evidence out of the Assertion tuple into an explicit typed relation (Supports/Contradicts/Qualifies/Weakens/Contextualizes between Evidence and Assertion) rather than embedding it as a field, since one assertion may be supported or contradicted by several distinct evidence items with different relation types.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero and Lord should not be components of Knowledge... Zero is an operation: Zero: K -> Z. Lord is an operation: Lord: K -> L.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms and generalizes the earlier circularity concern (from S0784): Zero and Lord must be typed as operations Zero:K->Z and Lord:K->L over the Knowledge State type K, never as stored fields of K itself; their outputs may be persisted as derived artifacts but are not foundational components of knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Entity | Dimension | Value | Proposition | Evidence | Epistemic State | Assertion | Relationship | Knowledge State | Knowledge Space ... a type system defines: what kinds of objects exist, what properties each has, how types relate, what operations are valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Answers the posed Question 7A by producing a complete ten-type system for KnowledgeOS (Entity, Dimension, Value, Proposition, Evidence, EpistemicState, Assertion, Relationship, KnowledgeState, KnowledgeSpace) with formal set-builder definitions, a type hierarchy diagram, per-type well-formedness constraints, and operation signatures (Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Compare/Challenge/Update/Preserve, all typed as maps between these object types).

a_rows_sample.anchor: WellTyped(K) = WellTypedObjects(K) and WellTypedRelationships(K) and ValidCardinalities(K) ... Supports(Evidence,Assertion) valid; Supports(Person,Assertion) invalid
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects WellTyped from a pure object-typing predicate to also require relationship typing and cardinality validity (e.g. Supports must relate Evidence to Assertion, not Person to Assertion), since syntactically valid objects can still violate relationship-type rules.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U = {E, D, V, P, A, R, E_v, Sigma, H, Z, L, K, I} ... this ontology is the foundation for all KnowledgeOS operations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 13-type universe (Entity, Dimension, Value, Proposition, Assertion, Relationship, Evidence, EpistemicState, History, ZeroFinding, LordCandidate, KnowledgeState, IdealState) with formal set-builder definitions, well-formedness predicates for Proposition/Assertion/Relationship, and an explicit epistemic lattice claim over the 2240-state Sigma space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: You later define Relationship separately... Relationship in Entity and Relationship in Relationship could become possible. Entity != Relationship.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Entity definition (which included 'relationship' as an example subject) for creating an ontological ambiguity where a Relationship could also be typed as an Entity; a relationship may become the subject of a proposition without itself being classified as an Entity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P=(E,D,V) ... too restrictive for the complete KnowledgeOS theory ... doesn't naturally represent 'Bhishma supports the Kaurava side' or 'Assertion A contradicts Assertion B' or 'Evidence E supports Assertion A' ... P=(S,rho,O,Gamma) ... AttributeProposition subset Proposition
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Entity+Dimension+Value proposition model as too narrow to represent relational/meta propositions (assertion-contradicts-assertion, evidence-supports-assertion); generalizes Proposition to a subject-predicate-object-qualifiers form P=(S,rho,O,Gamma), with the earlier attribute proposition recovered as the special case rho=hasDimension, so AttributeProposition becomes a subtype of Proposition rather than the whole of it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: To call something a lattice mathematically, you need a partial order such that every pair has lub and glb. You haven't defined that... Replace Transition Lattice with Epistemic State Space or Epistemic Transition System.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the claim that the epistemic state space (Sigma=A x S x R x V x C with a proposed preceq order) forms a mathematical lattice, since the required least-upper-bound/greatest-lower-bound structure was never established and the Resolution component (Open/InProgress/Resolved/Unresolvable) is not naturally ordered; downgrades the claim to an unstructured product state space pending proof of any lattice properties.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(E_v,P) in [-1,1] ... epistemically dangerous... I recommend replacing the primitive scalar with Bearing(E,P) in {Support,Contradict,Neutral,Irrelevant,Unknown} and separately Strength(E,P) in [0,1].
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the signed [-1,1] evidence-support scalar (0 could mean neutral, irrelevant, insufficient, unknown, or not-assessed -- these are not equivalent), replacing it with a categorical Bearing (Support/Contradict/Neutral/Irrelevant/Unknown) plus an optional separate numeric Strength.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An Assertion without evidence must be representable, otherwise Zero cannot represent a missing-evidence condition... Evidence(A) subseteq E_v and |Evidence(A)| >= 0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Assertion well-formedness rule that required a non-empty Evidence field, which would make MissingEvidence (an established Gap type) unrepresentable; an assertion's Evidence set must be allowed to be empty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: You use ~ for both Consistent (line 480) and Normative Conflict (line 488). That is unacceptable in a formal theory... A1 => A2 as causal... but => is conventionally logical implication. Causation != LogicalEntailment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags an actual notation error (the symbol ~ used for two different relationship types, Consistent and Normative Conflict, in the same table) and a symbol-overload error (=> used for causal implication when it conventionally denotes logical implication), recommending distinct notations and the explicit invariant Causation != LogicalEntailment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Content != EpistemicStatus != Evaluation ... Ontology -> Formal Semantics -> State Model -> Evaluation Algebra -> DDD Model -> Implementation, not Graph Schema -> Call it Ontology.

Validates the Zero Lens claim UNKNOWN≠ABSENT with a concrete formal witness: if Contr(p) and NoAssessment(p) both map to U, the representation has collapsed two semantically distinct situations, and this Representation_Collapse(Contr,Unknown) is now measurable.

a_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest possible outcome for the composition experiment as a separation witness: if M3(p∘q)≠M4(p∘q) under some legitimate composition rule, then M3 is not_sem-equivalent to M4 under that observable contract; conversely, if exhaustive composition over all declared operations gives M3(x,op)≅M4(x,op) for all x,op, the extra value is confirmed as merely representational relabeling for that semantic contract -- a powerful negative result either way.

b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the core scoring result: A/B/C each pass only 7/12 required distinctions, failing on the identical seven; D (structured evaluation) passes all 12. The seven common failures collapse the unknown family (Unobservable≡InsufficientEvidence≡Underdetermined≡TheoryIncomplete≡...→U), meaning adding a contradiction value does not address distinctions lying outside the contradiction dimension.

b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NextEpistemicAct(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,Pi) ... a_t in {Clarify, Search, Observe, ConsultResource, AssessEvidence, Determine, Defer, Act}. ... EA1..EA7
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a four-layer Epistemic Agency Execution Loop (front-end interaction; gap detection & classification via K_t|=Q; epistemic agency selection via a*=argmax[ExpectedGapReduction/(Cost+Risk)]; determination & output) and seven hypotheses EA1-EA7: EA1 observation!=interpretation; EA2 intent as unconfirmed hypothesis; EA3 typed gap resolution over {Semantic,Epistemic,...}; EA4 epistemic action optimization a*=argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost]; EA5 resource-bounded actions A_t=Filter(A,Resources_t); EA6 Lord/Sarathi duality (generate vs select); EA7 Determine(Evidence) before Act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t |= Q ... This notation is dangerous. ... Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) ... or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) ... should not become a new KnowledgeOS primitive. Use the existing vocabulary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the dangerous overloading of logical entailment notation K_t|=Q (which normally means semantic entailment, much stronger than intended) to the existing Adequacy/Determination vocabulary Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R), so as not to introduce a redundant new primitive, consistent with the established Determination!=Knowledge and Adequacy!=Determination!=Knowledge distinctions.

a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects freezing the four-way gap taxonomy {Semantic,Epistemic,Resource,Policy} as exhaustive; recommends Delta_Q(K_t) as a typed collection of unsatisfied requirements with a ClassifyGap:Delta_Q->G mapping where G remains research-open, illustrated by four metro-scenario gap readings (inquiry gap, knowledge gap, resource gap, decision/policy gap).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap -> Opportunity -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution ... Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action. That distinction should remain intact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates four conflated concerns in the original design (what is missing, what can be done, what should be done, what is allowed) into an explicit chain Delta_t -> A_t^possible -> A_t^feasible -> a_t* -> Authorization(a_t*) -> Execute(a_t*), preserving the existing Proposal!=Decision!=Authorization!=Action distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a_t^* = argmax_{a in A_t^feasible} EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) ... KnowledgeOS should not assume that epistemic information gain is always the objective.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA4's argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost] formula as an insufficient decision rule (pure info-gain/cost could select an unsafe action, and sometimes not acting is optimal), generalizing to a_t*=argmax EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) without freezing the exact utility formula, and abstracting the capability as NextEpistemicAct:(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,C_t,EC_t)->A_t to be determined experimentally.

a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA5's simple Filter(A,Resources_t) model to a richer per-resource state Resource_t(r)=(Availability,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...), making Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) meaningful and connecting to the existing evidence-channel work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: unless your actual observation included a specified probability model, that inequality is not established. Likewise "maintaining eye contact" was not part of the original factual description. ... Never move directly O -> P(H) without specifying the inference model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags that the worked human trace contains invented (unobserved) details treated as facts (e.g. an unstated probability inequality, 'maintaining eye contact', 'language barrier'), violating the very Observation!=Interpretation discipline KnowledgeOS is meant to enforce; recommends explicitly labeling O(observed)/I(interpretation)/H(hypothesis)/P(probability output) and never moving directly from O to P(H) without a specified inference model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q_0 -> Clarification -> Q_1 -> Clarification -> Q_2 ... until WellFormed(Q_n,C) and only then Gap(Q_n,K_t). ... Inquiry Formation ... distinct from Inquiry Resolution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the pipeline with a multi-cycle Inquiry Formation stage (Q0->Clarification->Q1->...->WellFormed(Q_n,C)) preceding gap analysis, explicitly distinguished from Inquiry Resolution; illustrated by the metro example needing a follow-up clarifying question ('Where are you going?') before the direction question is answerable.

a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA7 (universal Determine-before-Act) by distinguishing three action classes (epistemic actions like search/inspect/ask which may precede determination; operational actions requiring determination+authorization; safety/emergency actions taken under uncertainty), giving the conditional rule 'required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination', preserving Epistemic Decision != Operational Decision != Authorization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a metaphor can expose a structure without proving that the metaphor names an architectural component. ... [PROP] Lord/Sarathi is an interpretive naming lens for the two functions; not a canonical architectural name.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demotes EA6's Lord/Sarathi naming to CandidateGenerator(K_t,Delta_t,R_t)->A_t and ActionSelector(K_t,Delta_t,A_t,C_t,EC_t)->a_t, tagging Lord/Sarathi as merely [PROP] interpretive naming, invoking the prior Gita governance lesson that a metaphor can expose a structure without naming an architectural component.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract? ... A new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required capability absent from the current model, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the kernel question from 'should Epistemic Agency become a kernel operator' to 'does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract', restating the standing rule that a new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required absent capability, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation equivalence not-implies Intent equivalence ... Good action selection not-implies Correct knowledge ... Resource availability not-implies Resource reliability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a controlled factorial benchmark (fixed K_t,Q,Delta while varying resources R_t across cases A-D, then epistemic standards/risk/inquiry across cases E-G, expecting A*_A!=A*_B!=A*_C!=A*_D when resources materially differ) plus two adversarial experiments: a 'wrong assumption' test with four worlds sharing an identical observation but different underlying intent, giving Observation equivalence does not imply Intent equivalence; and a 'wrong resource' test where good action selection leads to a wrong search result, giving Good action selection does not imply Correct knowledge and Resource availability does not imply Resource reliability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a) = E[U_gap(a)] - C_resource(a) - Omega_risk(a) + U_task(a) ... the additive form is not theoretically established. ... EU = F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task) as the general specification, and treat the additive version as [PROP] EU_additive.
a_rows_sample.statement: The draft's additive four-term utility decomposition EU(a)=E[U_gap(a)]-C_resource(a)-Omega_risk(a)+U_task(a) is corrected to a general (unestablished-form) specification EU=F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task), with the additive version relegated to [PROP] EU_additive pending experimental validation, since e.g. risk may interact with epistemic benefit rather than subtract independently.

a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects assuming a generic norm ||Delta||_G over the gap space, since typed gaps (missing value, missing dimension, contradiction, insufficient evidence, unobservable quantity, underdetermination, model insufficiency, semantic ambiguity) do not naturally form a vector space; replaces it with a general candidate gap-value/reduction function U_gap(a)=V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a;Q,C,EC,S), with an actual metric d(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}) introduced only if experiments establish a numerical structure.

b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zoom-out from mere restoration (FocusedState->OriginalState) to Integration: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t)=Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t), diagnosing that prior Zoom-out experiments struggled because they attempted to classify Zoom-out before separating restoration from integration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn = search for potentially relevant structure ... Zero = test eliminability of represented structure. ... ZoomIn discovers and Zero tests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Zoom-in and Zero as complementary operations relative to the same (Q,C,Pi,S): Zoom-in searches for potentially relevant structure (discovers), Zero tests eliminability of represented structure (tests); a candidate pipeline ZoomIn->ExpandedRepresentation->ZeroLens->RelevantSubspace->FactFinding is proposed but explicitly not assumed to be a fixed order, tagged [PROP] not axiom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: projection to different observation field ... I would be careful. ... Unless we have pi^2=pi or an appropriate semantic projection definition, don't call every Zoom-in a projection. Use inquiry-relative view transformation ... or focus transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against calling every Zoom-in operation a mathematical 'projection' unless an established idempotent projection structure (pi^2=pi) or semantic-projection definition is demonstrated; recommends 'inquiry-relative view transformation' or 'focus transformation' as neutral terminology, consistent with the Zero Algebra lesson to discover the algebra rather than impose it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn: Where should I investigate? EpistemicAgency: What should I do next? FactFinding: What does the evidence establish? ZoomOut: How does the finding change the broader state?
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four distinct research questions into a coherent architecture: ZoomIn (where should I investigate), Epistemic Agency (what should I do next), Fact Finding (what does the evidence establish), Zoom-out (how does the finding change the broader state), combined into Observation->Relevance->ZoomIn->DimensionDiscovery->FactFinding->Determination->ZoomOut->Integration->K_{t+1} with a feedback loop from DimensionDiscovery back to NewObservation->NewZoomIn.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 ... ZF1 -- Context preservation ... ZF2 -- Dimension expansion ... ZF3 -- Cross-boundary discovery ... ZF4 -- Determination dependence ... ZF5 -- Investigation != determination ... ZF6 -- Zoom-out integration ... ZF7 -- Resource/agency interaction
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 with seven candidate hypotheses: ZF1 ZoomIn(K_t,Q) does not imply Delete(K_t); ZF2 D_t subseteq D_{t+1} can occur through investigation; ZF3 a relevant dimension need not be contained in the initial observation's representation; ZF4 newly discovered dimensions can change Determine(Q); ZF5 ZoomIn != Determine; ZF6 a finding discovered during Zoom-in can modify the broader state; ZF7 the next investigated dimension depends on K,Q,Delta,Resources,Context,Contract,Risk.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Backup -> large transfer, GitLab Runner -> large transfer, Replication -> large transfer ... the system must not say I found GitLab Runner, therefore GitLab Runner is the cause. ... No Determination Without Alternative Space.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses a multi-cause Nexus-egress failure case (Backup, GitLab Runner, and Replication all plausibly producing large transfer) to argue against single-hypothesis-collapse ('I found X, therefore X is the cause'), requiring the full hypothesis set H_Q to undergo Evidence Assessment before Determination, stated as the principle 'No Determination Without Alternative Space.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_t -> ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q) -> D_t subseteq D_{t+1} -> Acquire -> Assess -> Determine -> ZoomOut(Finding,K_t) -> K_{t+1} ... Terminology Correction: View Transformation vs. Projection
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a four-level Decoupled Dimensional Expansion & Integration Pipeline (1. Observation Entry O_t={d_0}; 2. Dimensional Discovery ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q)->D_t subseteq D_{t+1}; 3. Fact-Finding Acquire->Assess->Determine; 4. Integration ZoomOut(Finding,K_t)->K_{t+1}), and replaces the term 'projection' with 'Inquiry-Directed View Transformation' to avoid assuming idempotence (pi^2=pi) prior to empirical discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t <=_O Focus(K_t,Q) where <=_O means that the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable. ... ZF1 -- Context Preservation: Zoom-In changes inquiry focus without itself removing or invalidating surrounding Knowledge State.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF1's undefined comparison ZoomIn(K_t,Q)!=Delete(K_t) to K_t<=_O Focus(K_t,Q), where <=_O means the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable, avoiding accidentally turning Zoom-In into an undefined representation-theoretic operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Discovery of a dimension != acceptance of that dimension into Knowledge State. ... exactly analogous to your existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge. ... ZF2 -- Dimensional Expansion: Inquiry-directed investigation can introduce candidate explanatory dimensions not represented in the initial active representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF2's D_t subset D_{t+1} (which conflates dimension discovery with state evolution) by introducing D_t^cand as candidate dimensional space distinct from D_t^rep (accepted into Knowledge State), giving D_t^rep subseteq D_{t+1}^cand and a later integration D_{t+1}^cand -> D_{t+1}^rep, analogous to the existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(I_t) ... ZF3 currently risks becoming tautological ... GitLab Runner may already exist somewhere in the Knowledge Graph but not be connected to the egress observation. That is not dimensional discovery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF3's under-specified d* not-in Rep(O_t) (risking tautology) by distinguishing not-observable-in-O_t, not-represented-in-K_t, and genuinely-discovered-during-investigation, requiring d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(investigation trace I_t), noting a dimension already present elsewhere in the graph but unconnected to the observation does not count as dimensional discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) != Determine(K'_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) with K'_t = Expand(K_t,d*). ... Otherwise a change in determination could simply result from changing standards, evidence, inquiry, or reasoning regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF4 (Determine(Q|D_t)!=Determine(Q|D')) to hold the full determination signature Q,C,EC,S,R fixed and intervene only on the discovered dimensional representation, giving Determine(K_t,...)!=Determine(K'_t,...) with K'_t=Expand(K_t,d*), so the change is attributable to dimensional expansion alone rather than confounded with standards/evidence/inquiry/reasoning-regime changes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Zoom-In that discovers ... has succeeded even if Fact-Finding concludes: Cause remains underdetermined. So: DiscoverySuccess not-implies Determination should probably become a candidate invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retains and operationally sharpens ZF5 (ZoomIn:(K_t,O_t,Q)->D^cand versus FactFinding:(D^cand,E,H_Q,M,S)->Standing->Determination), proposing the candidate invariant DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination: Zoom-In can succeed in surfacing candidates even when Fact-Finding concludes the cause remains underdetermined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut should not be defined as ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t. That would recreate the old restoration model. Instead: ZoomOut(F,K_t) = Integrate(K_t,F) -> K_{t+1} ... ZoomOut = integration of finding rather than: ZoomOut = inverse(ZoomIn).
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids defining Zoom-Out as the inverse of Zoom-In (ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t would recreate the old restoration model); Zoom-Out is Integrate(K_t,F)->K_{t+1} where F may contain newly discovered dimensions, assessed evidence, determined relationships, rejected hypotheses, unresolved alternatives, provenance, and temporal information, so K_{t+1}!=K_t may occur even though Zoom-In itself deleted nothing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* in ArgMax_{d in D^cand} E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d) as a candidate agency policy, not a kernel law. ... ZoomIn != Agency. Agency selects the next investigation; Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF7's dimension-selection formula (which assumed Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions are comparably valued, costs are scalarizable, and an argmax exists) to an explicitly candidate agency policy d* in ArgMax_{d}E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d), not a kernel law, reaffirming ZoomIn != Agency (Agency selects the next investigation, Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZF8 -- Representation Boundary Non-Closure ... An initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions. ... ZF3 asks: Can the relevant dimension cross the initial boundary? ZF8 asks: Is the initial dimensional representation itself epistemically non-closed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds ZF8 (Representation Boundary Non-Closure): the initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions, distinguished from ZF3 (can a relevant dimension cross the boundary) by asking instead whether the initial representation is itself epistemically non-closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zoom-In != Zero != Fact-Finding ... Determination ... Zoom-Out ... Epistemic Agency ... This is much more promising than trying to make Zoom-In or Zoom-Out kernel primitives.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a six-way functional separation as the architectural conclusion: Zoom-In (expand/search the inquiry space) != Zero Lens (determine what can be eliminated while preserving contract) != Fact-Finding (establish what evidence supports) != Determination (establish what can be decided under the epistemic regime) != Zoom-Out (integrate finding into broader state) != Epistemic Agency (select what to investigate/do next); recommends testing ZF2+ZF3+ZF5 first as the foundational experiment before the rest of the architecture is tested.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not one function that maps knowledge directly to truth ... typed epistemic pipeline: Representation\rightarrow Reasoning\rightarrow Derivation\rightarrow Evaluation\rightarrow Determination\rightarrow Decision\rightarrow Transition ... while Explanation remains a separate abductive path.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline theoretical insight, restated by both the proposal and the approving HPA advisory: 'KnowledgeOS is not one function that maps knowledge directly to truth; it is a typed epistemic pipeline: Representation -> Reasoning -> Derivation -> Evaluation -> Determination -> Decision -> Transition', with Explanation as a separate abductive path (K_t,O_t)--Explain-->H_t; this fills a structural hole without prematurely solving Contr, phi, R_req, >=(preceq/succeq), ≡sem, lifecycle, Zero or delta, all of which remain OPEN, and does not modify frozen Theory v1.2.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O-A zoom-out with no investigation between in and out ... K_{t+1}=K_t exactly. O-B zoom-out after an investigation that determined nothing ... O-C zoom-out after an investigation that determined a decoy ... O-D n-cycle round trip with no new evidence ... fidelity must stay 1.000 ... O-E paired seeds
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares, in advance, six named controls for KR-ZOOM-OUT-01: O-A (null round-trip with no investigation, expecting exact K_{t+1}=K_t), O-B (zoom-out after an investigation that determined nothing, expecting empty discoveries), O-C (zoom-out after determining a decoy, must be distinguishable from determining the true cause), O-D (an n-cycle round trip with no new evidence, expecting fidelity to stay 1.000, with any decay attributed to a harness defect rather than information loss), O-E (paired seeds across in/out orders, isolating order effects from sample effects), and O-F (a degenerate-metric pre-check requiring, for every metric, a named case that would give it a different value, with metrics lacking such a case dropped before the run) -- O-F explicitly named as the direct institutionalization of the H3c failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verify that T(D) yields a valid non-trivial state transformation. ... A non-trivial transformation does not guarantee that the actual Zero estimand can vary. We already learned this from KR-ZOOM-OUT-03. ... the declared VARIABLE estimand e must have at least one admissible witness before freeze. And
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the O-F* degeneracy check for this protocol, explicitly citing the lesson already learned from KR-ZOOM-OUT-03: verifying only that the transformation T(D) is non-trivial is too weak, since a non-trivial transformation does not guarantee the actual estimand of interest can vary; requires instead that every declared VARIABLE estimand have at least one admissible witness before the protocol is frozen, and that any intentionally constant estimand be explicitly declared CONSTANT rather than tested as though variable -- listing 8 specific quantities in this protocol that must each pass this stronger check.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D15. step-025g (183746) -- Formal Lord Algebra ... section6 action utility vector A=(Purpose,ExpectedGain,Cost,Risk,Urgency,Reversibility,Authorization,Dependencies,Deadline) ... section19 Prefer(a1,a2|K,G,C) rather than Score(a) ... section24 the default Lord policy ... section54 commissions 025H (Sarathi)
a_rows_sample.statement: Step-025g (file 183746) formalizes Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,C) -> a_t, splitting Action into EpistemicAction (q: K_t -> K_{t+1}) and OperationalAction (a: W_t -> W_{t+1}) under the rule 'Lord selects; Governance authorizes; Executor executes'; rejects a^*=argmax VOI(a) as insufficient and instead defines a nine-dimension action utility vector A=(Purpose,ExpectedGain,Cost,Risk,Urgency,Reversibility,Authorization,Dependencies,Deadline), explicitly refusing a collapsed scalar Score(A) that 'would hide semantics'; uses a two-stage feasibility-then-optimization algorithm and root-gap analysis (graph reasoning, not LLM intuition); offers an optional statistical expected-utility engine but favors a qualitative preference relation Prefer(a1,a2|K,G,C) (deliberately arg-prefer, not arg-max-Score, 'we have not yet established that these dimensions can legitimately be collapsed'); states Capability != Authority; states the default Lord policy verbatim ('prefer the least risky authorized action that maximally reduces decision-critical Zero, subject to cost, dependencies and deadlines'); defines a termination algebra {Completed,Blocked,Escalated,Abandoned,Expired} with DoNothing in ActionSpace and 'no action is preferable to an unjustified action'; runs five experiments and six falsification passes, including the finding that high information value cannot override governance and that an LLM recommendation cannot override Zero/Contract; and commissions Sarathi (step-025H) as the next research item, delivered the following day outside this batch.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GAPS AT BATCH END ... 4. EC naming issue open ... 5. Zero's EC construction ... The chain terminates in an acknowledged human boundary, not a computed one. ... 7. Sarathi is unformalised in this batch -- commissioned at 025g section54 as step-025H, delivered on 2026-08-28.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists seven gaps remaining at the end of the batch: no aggregation operator selected; evidence identity unresolved; circular derivation handling unresolved; the EC naming issue (Epistemic-Governance Contract vs AssuranceContract) left open; Zero's contract-construction machinery (ContractDerivation, RequirementGraph) handed through 025e/025f to a chain that terminates in an acknowledged human-governance boundary rather than a computed resolution; no executed property-based test of the knowledge-state machine itself (only the evidence algebra was empirically tested, and that CSV lives at a non-repository sandbox path); and Sarathi remains entirely unformalised in this batch, commissioned at step-025g section 54 as step-025H but actually delivered the following day (2026-08-28), meaning any Sarathi record must be sourced from batch B5, not B4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 25G.24 (verbatim): a* = arg prefer_{a in A} [GapReduction, Safety, Authorization, Cost, Urgency, Reversibility] -- NOT a well-defined operator. ... 25G.36 step5 "Rank by decision-critical gap reduction" ... implicitly counting gaps, which directly contradicts 25D.17 ("the six missing items are not necessarily comparable... Zero is primarily a structured object, not a scalar"). This is the sharpest intra-band contradiction (VA-2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the sharpest intra-band contradiction (VA-2): step-025g's action-selection operator a* = arg-prefer over a six-dimensional codomain (GapReduction, Safety, Authorization, Cost, Urgency, Reversibility) is not a well-defined operator -- no order, lexicographic priority, Pareto rule, or aggregation is given, which the source itself concedes ('we have not yet established that these dimensions can legitimately be collapsed'); yet the very next section's worked ranking step implicitly counts gaps (GapReduction(a3) > GapReduction(a1) because a3 closes two gaps versus one), directly contradicting step-025d's own explicit claim that gaps 'are not necessarily comparable' and that 'Zero is primarily a structured object, not a scalar.' The result is that Lord's central ranking mechanism depends on exactly the operation Zero's own formalization declares undefined or forbidden.

a_rows_sample.anchor: (b) Operator signature drift ... Revise/Revision/F/T/Update: seven surface forms for the transition operator; base delta: K x O_K -harpoon-> K never cited. ... Lord ... Output type drifts set->scalar-choice->record.
a_rows_sample.statement: Catalogues operator signature drift within the same 14-file band: the knowledge-state transition operator surfaces in seven distinct forms (Update, Revise, Revision, F, T, a second Revision, a second Update) never citing the base corpus's delta:K x O_K -harpoon-> K; Lord's output type drifts from a generated set of possibilities (step-025b) to an optimizer's argmax ratio (step-025c-3) to a policy-governed single-action selector emitting a DecisionState record (step-025g); Sarathi is given two incompatible arities within the single file step-025b and is never formalized anywhere in the band; the Commit predicate and the Assessment/evidence-state object each surface in multiple incompatible shapes (Assessment alone has seven distinct shapes); and the same symbol (direct-sum) denotes evidence combination in one file and 'structured collection, not numerical addition' in another.

a_rows_sample.statement: Documents contradiction VB-1: the 19-file band opens (step-025h) with Sarathi as the deciding agent (a five-way DecisionResult codomain including Decision itself) and Lord as the next-action selector, but closes (step-025z) with Lord explicitly named 'Epistemic Decision and Action Orchestrator' owning Decide among its options, while Sarathi is demoted to specializing in Reasoning/Planning/Interpretation/OptionGeneration only -- a full role reversal relative to the band's own opening file, pivoting through step-025r's remark that the Lord/Sarathi boundary 'is a DDD design decision', with no file ever acknowledging the swap occurred.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero != Lord != Sarathi != Transition ... K_t -Zero-> Z_t -Lord-> L_t -Sarathi-> a_t -Commit-> e_t -delta-> K_{t+1} ... Zero, Lord, and Sarathi do not change K
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the initial Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Commit/Transition pipeline as a linear sequence culminating in a state change, with explicit invariants that Zero, Lord and Sarathi are each analytical (never transformational) and none of their outputs alone entail K_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi should not 'recommend Commit'... Commitment is not an epistemic action. It is an authorization/governance action... a_t -Authorize-> c_t -Execute-> e_t. Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Removes 'Commit' from Sarathi's action vocabulary and inserts an explicit Authorization boundary between recommendation and execution: Sarathi produces a recommendation a_t, Authorize(Knower,a_t,Policy) produces a command c_t, Execute(c_t) produces an event e_t, and only then does delta(K_t,e_t) fire -- Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition, with the missing Authorize function explicitly making the Knower's authority mathematically visible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Execute: C -> E is too deterministic. Execution can fail... Execute(c_t) -> ExecutionResult in {Success(e),Failure(f),Partial(e,f)} ... ExecutionResult != DomainEvent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Execute from a total deterministic function C->E to one returning a structured ExecutionResult (Success/Failure/Partial), and similarly Authorize to return an AuthorizationResult (Authorized/Rejected/Deferred/Modified) rather than assuming every recommendation becomes a command; ExecutionResult is explicitly distinguished from the DomainEvent that actually triggers a transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the epistemic cycle is actually not always a cycle... External observation -> Event -> Transition can update the state directly... Guidance is optional; Transition is fundamental. G5 - Guidance is not a prerequisite for transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the closing theorem G5: Guidance (Zero/Lord/Sarathi) is not a prerequisite for every Knowledge-State transition -- a raw external observation event or a scheduled validity check can trigger delta(K_t,e_t) directly, so the lenses must never be modelled as mandatory middleware sitting between every event and the transition function; renames the pipeline from 'Epistemic Cycle' to 'Epistemic Guidance-and-Transition Cycle' to reflect this.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi \rightarrow DecisionPosture
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sarathi's output from a binary Stop/Continue decision to a richer DecisionPosture ∈ {Proceed, Investigate, ProceedWithCaveats, Defer, Escalate, UnableToDecide}, argued to be closer to Sarathi's actual role.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation \neq Assertion
b_rows_sample.statement: Strict boundary: Recommendation ≠ Assertion, Recommendation ≠ Fact, Recommendation ≠ Decision. Sārathi may say 'Investigate the moral obligation dimension' but KnowledgeOS must not silently convert that into 'Therefore Arjuna should fight' — the Knower remains the decision authority unless the domain explicitly delegates that authority. Marked as extremely important for the DDD model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Lord needs a stronger boundary too: Candidate ≠ Knowledge, Candidate ≠ Evidence, Candidate ≠ Assertion. A presentation should visually distinguish KNOWN / INFERRED / UNKNOWN / CANDIDATE / RECOMMENDED to prevent semantic contamination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(S_t) \rightarrow EpistemicFindings
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Zero's role as boundary-finder, not belief-decider: Zero(S_t) -> EpistemicFindings, Presentation ⊇ DecisionRelevant(EpistemicFindings); 'Zero does not decide what the Knower should believe. Zero says: Here is where the state has a boundary.' Also strengthens provenance: EveryDecisionRelevantClaim -> Provenance, with a worked claim-level provenance record example (Acquisition/Evidence/Observed-at/Validity/Conflict/Source).

Unknown

b_rows_sample.statement: Elevates 'unknown' to a fundamental principle already implicit in Zero: Unknown ≠ Absent ≠ NotApplicable ≠ NotObserved ≠ NotYetInvestigated, illustrated by Version=UNKNOWN not meaning Version=ABSENT, and SecurityStatus=NOT_ASSESSED not meaning SecurityStatus=SAFE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq UniversalValidator
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD warning that Zero risks becoming a 'god object' by owning detection of gaps, conflicts, type problems, temporal problems and epistemic boundaries all at once: Zero ≠ UniversalValidator. Zero is redefined narrowly as detecting epistemic boundaries/deficiencies relevant to current state and purpose, aggregating epistemic consequences of findings from separate domain validators (schema, type, policy, security violations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: LordCandidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: LordCandidate ≠ Knowledge and LordCandidate ≠ Evidence: Lord can propose 'there may be a moral-obligation dimension' but it becomes knowledge only after investigation; critical to prevent AI-generated hypotheses entering the Knowledge State as facts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S\bar{a}rathiRecommendation \neq Decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Sārathi needs a constitutional policy boundary: SārathiRecommendation ≠ Decision, SārathiAction ≠ HumanAuthorization — Sārathi may determine the next best investigation, but the Knower decides whether to accept it unless the system has explicitly delegated authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (K,U,N,\Delta,P,Role) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action as too simplistic: Sārathi:(K,U,N,Δ,P,Role) -> Guidance, which may then produce Decision, which may then authorize Action, giving Guidance ≠ Decision ≠ Action (confirming an earlier DDD warning). Also reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as three functions/lenses over the state rather than three sequential stages: Zero=Diagnose, Lord=Reason/Synthesize/Orient, Sārathi=Guide, with Decision->Action occurring outside those lenses; explicitly an architectural abstraction, not a literal theological equivalence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (State, Norms, Role, Context, Discrepancies) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action (too direct) to Sārathi:(State,Norms,Role,Context,Discrepancies)->Guidance -> CandidateActions -> Decision -> Action, giving proper separation of concerns. Reaffirms Zero as a pure DiagnosticFunction that must not itself decide ('therefore do X'). Corrects Lord from 'merely a reasoning engine/LLM reasoning' to AuthoritativeKnowledge+NormativeOrientation+InterpretiveResolution, since Krishna in the text functions as an authoritative source of teaching, not just an inference engine — called crucial for KnowledgeOS governance. Confirms Sārathi = ContextualGuidance, distinguishing Lord ('what is authoritative/true/normative') from Sārathi ('how does that apply here') from Decision ('what will I choose') from Action ('what will I actually do').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K,I,C,P) \rightarrow \text{Epistemic Boundaries}
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as product capabilities rather than domain entities: Zero(K,I,C,P)->Epistemic Boundaries acts as an 'epistemic diagnostic engine' (missing dimensions, unknown values, missing/weak/conflicting evidence, logical contradictions, stale knowledge, contextual mismatches, unresolved questions, unsupported assumptions, Ideal-State discrepancies); Lord asks 'what else might matter?' enabling 'horizon expansion' beyond gap-checking; Sārathi:(K,I,Z,L,Q,C)->NextAction performs 'epistemic navigation', worked through a Bhīṣma-relationship example (Zero flags unknown relationship, Lord flags kinship as material, Sārathi recommends investigating it before evaluating the decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can we migrate this Nexus installation?
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: asked 'Can we migrate this Nexus installation?', a conventional AI answers directly, while KnowledgeOS first constructs required dimensions (version, repository inventory, blob stores, storage, network, DNS, firewall, certificates, backup, dependencies, authentication, operational constraints), runs Zero to find missing items (backup verification, firewall confirmation, certificate ownership, dependency inventory), and has Sārathi respond 'Do not decide migration readiness yet. Investigate these four items.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: perform justified action given epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C) \rightarrow EvidenceCandidates
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects plain Retrieve(Query)->Documents to a goal-directed Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C)->EvidenceCandidates: the retrieval system 'knows why it is retrieving', discovering relevant dimensions (e.g. version, repository topology, blob stores, firewall, certificates for a migration decision) before retrieving. Zero can drive retrieval: given a partially-filled knowledge-state checklist, Zero reports specific gaps (backup verification, firewall rules, certificate ownership) and Sārathi generates a concrete investigation plan (search infrastructure docs for backup configuration, etc.), giving Zero -> Gap -> Sārathi -> Retrieval as part of the investigation loop, not a one-shot lookup.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Zero}(K_t)\rightarrow\text{epistemic boundary}
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero continuously reveals 'what is still unknown' (Zero(K_t)->G_t, G_0->G_1->...); ideally G_t->∅, but if the knowledge space is genuinely unbounded Zero may never establish G_t=∅. The stronger concept is Zero(K_t)->epistemic boundary, with Moksha representing the boundary itself being transcended rather than merely all currently detected gaps being filled — judged 'much more profound'.

a_rows_sample.statement: Of a prior review's four 'remaining discoveries', three are already done: platform invariants (the 11-invariant set, 10 surviving cross-product projection), lifecycle owners (the Engineering Progression Model P-1..P-10, each with owner), and the Engineering Kernel (A-5, tested and falsified for sufficiency at n=1, MVK). a_rows_sample.statement: Three amendments: (1) the 'nine kinds' are held as candidate archetypes, not frozen primitives, until MM-1 resolves whether KIND is itself a dimension; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE, since its distinguishing edge ('generates Projections') is observed in only one space (the EKP) and nesting is unevidenced (H-3); (3) PURPOSE is flagged for its own investigation (U-MM-4, waits on D-5).

a_rows_sample.anchor: VERDICT: SUPPORTED — a meta-model HAS emerged. But not the one hypothesized. It is DIMENSIONAL-WITH-ARCHETYPES, not a flat category list
a_rows_sample.statement: Five independent classification passes (RQ-002 Knowledge Meta-Model; Engineering Platform Knowledge Metamodel; L-A knowledge-types.yaml; Relationship Ontology section 2; Progression Model), produced months apart by different exercises, converge on a dimensional-with-archetypes structure rather than a flat category list, refuting the hypothesized A-G flat list — the same error RQ-002 already refuted ('one thing cannot change type by being encoded differently').

a_rows_sample.statement: The candidate meta-model: an element of KnowledgeOS = KIND (archetype) x the RQ-002 dimensions (NATURE x REPRESENTATION x GOVERNANCE-STATUS x AUTHORITY-SCOPE, plus two candidate additions EVIDENCE-STATUS x OPERATIONAL-STATE). a_rows_sample.statement: The kinds themselves belong to KnowledgeOS (the meta-model is platform knowledge; a different adopter inherits the kinds, not the instances); instances distribute by AUTHORITY-SCOPE, which is why scope must remain a dimension; Runtime Assets are already bounded by R-42 (platform assets only); outside the platform lies external obligations (the CONSTRAINS gap, CV-3/G-3) which the meta-model inherits but does not fill.

a_rows_sample.statement: Five gaps classified by category (Structural/Behavioral/Evolutionary) and cause: G-1 (I-4/ATTESTS/PROJECTION inert-vs-attested) is EVOLUTIONARY, caused by a missing lifecycle, belongs to LIFECYCLE. G-2 (SPECIALIZES, Engineering Knowledge -> product knowledge) is EVOLUTIONARY, a missing relationship, belongs to ONTOLOGY. a_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ANNOTATED 2026-08-02 — THREE CORRECTIONS ... LEVEL MIXING — my third instance of that error class
a_rows_sample.statement: Three annotated corrections (recorded in KnowledgeOS_Relationship_Ontology.md): (1) section 2's six concepts are not siblings but four ontological layers (Purpose/Mission, Platform/Capability+Knowledge, Representation/Artifact, Application/PKS+Product) listed as one set — a third instance of level mixing; (2) PKS is a CONTAINER, not a layer below ARTIFACT — a PKS contains artifacts, and KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted as the container concept, defined by a declared boundary (scope.include), not a folder; (3) the document itself conflates two levels — section 1 (dimensions) is a meta-model, section 2 (concepts) is an ontology, both named rather than the whole renamed. a_rows_sample.statement: Four existing dimensions admitted, each tested against orthogonal/necessary: D-I NATURE (what kind of thing it is, from RQ-002); D-II REPRESENTATION (how it is encoded, from RQ-002, proved orthogonal by RQ-002's smoking gun that the same rule landed in different types depending on encoding); D-III GOVERNANCE-STATUS (lifecycle position, from RQ-002 + statuses.yaml's 8 executable values); D-IV AUTHORITY-SCOPE (how far it reaches, from RQ-002 + ES-005.1's three concerns + placement scopes).

a_rows_sample.statement: Two new dimensions are admitted: D-V EVIDENCE-STATUS (observed/inferred/hypothesized; not a field anywhere but necessary because ten rediscoveries and four falsifications happened because claims were not graded); D-VI OPERATIONAL-STATE (enforced/advisory/unexercised; implied by deny/ask/hooks but never formalized, necessary because it is what '0 traversals' and a prior '0 of 11 enforcing' error both measured badly).

a_rows_sample.anchor: INTENT-STATUS ... REJECT ... It fails orthogonality ... "Ratified" and "approved" are the same axis
a_rows_sample.statement: A proposed INTENT-STATUS dimension (proposed/sponsor-intended/ratified/operational) is rejected: it fails orthogonality because statuses.yaml already runs draft->discovery->reviewed->approved->baseline->frozen->superseded->archived, so 'ratified' and 'approved' are the same axis, 'proposed' is draft, 'operational' is baseline. It decomposes into INTENT = (GOVERNANCE-STATUS x OWNER); 'sponsor intent' is simply governance-status draft/approved with owner:sponsor. Applying the same rule that rejected INTENDED to this proposal is treated as a consistency requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE CANONICAL MODEL — six dimensions, four existing, two new, one rejected ... KnowledgeOS instance = NATURE × REPRESENTATION × GOVERNANCE-STATUS × AUTHORITY-SCOPE × EVIDENCE-STATUS × OPERATIONAL-STATE
a_rows_sample.statement: The canonical model: a KnowledgeOS instance = NATURE x REPRESENTATION x GOVERNANCE-STATUS x AUTHORITY-SCOPE x EVIDENCE-STATUS x OPERATIONAL-STATE. Derived (never axes, extending RQ-002's rule by one): lifecycle regime = f(NATURE); validation method = f(REPRESENTATION, NATURE); intent = f(GOVERNANCE-STATUS, OWNER). Evidence, Intent, Governance and Operational State are separated as required, but Intent is separated by derivation, not by adding an axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Success-criterion test — six real artifacts classified ... All six classify. And the test produced a finding on its own: Round39-MC is frozen yet ENFORCED, while CAP-001 is realized yet only advisory
a_rows_sample.statement: Six real artifacts (CAP-001 README, Round39-MC, a verification report, PKS_..._M4, settings.json deny, this document) were classified across all six dimensions without altering the model. The test independently proved orthogonality: Round39-MC is frozen (governance-status) yet enforced (operational-state), while CAP-001 is realized yet only advisory — governance-status and operational-state vary independently, obtained by using the model rather than arguing for it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Platform Lifecycle (Idea→Knowledge→PKS→Implementation→Evidence→Evolution) ... B-1 correction: software→evidence OBSERVED · back-edge n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal · KnowledgeOS→PKS n=0 · Genesis has NO route
b_rows_sample.statement: The platform lifecycle is graded link-by-link: software-to-evidence is observed; the back-edge is n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal; KnowledgeOS-to-PKS generation is n=0; and the Genesis stage has no route at all. b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-6: KnowledgeOS creates PKS. External support: scaffolding/generators (Spring Initializr-class) are implementation guidance only; context-engineering platforms that auto-assemble context are adjacent. Challenge: no external instance of generating a governed knowledge space is found; internally n=0. Confidence: UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven both inside and outside the corpus.

b_rows_sample.statement: Three corrections applied to the (external) concept matrix: (1) 'PKS = Context Engineering' softened to 'PKS addresses the same problem space as context engineering and extends it with governance, lifecycle, authority and engineering semantics' — not an identity claim, since the governed form has no demonstrated external instance; (2) Jansen & Bosch elevated to primary validation, since it validates the PROBLEM (knowledge vaporizes), and problem validation outranks solution fashion (Gartner-era context engineering); (3) the admission rule adopted as a standing header rule on both matrices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship pass sharpens the concept pass's conclusion: the platform's EDGES are almost all standard engineering — what is uniquely unproven is ONE edge (creates → PKS) and ONE layer name (DP-n)
b_rows_sample.statement: Aggregate result: externally supported (>=HIGH) relationships are R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8, R-10, and R-2's separation; medium relationships are R-1, R-7, R-9; the unique, operationally-unproven items are R-6 (creates->PKS) and DP-n as a named layer. The distinctive bet of KnowledgeOS is now precisely locatable as R-6; everything else is either validated or a naming choice, and R-6 is exactly what the charter's gated stages and the docket's doors already refuse to assume.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — R-6 BROADENED per review: the bet is the INTEGRATION, not one edge
b_rows_sample.statement: Challenge accepted: 'KnowledgeOS is not merely a generator. It is the platform that governs the ENTIRE PKS lifecycle.' R-6 is restated as a composite chain: KnowledgeOS discovers/models/governs/generates/evolves PKS, guides PRODUCT ENGINEERING (the actor — work, not magic), which engineers software, collects evidence, and improves KnowledgeOS. The actor (product engineering) was already implicit in the work-execution progressions (P-7/P-8) and 'the producing track' as records-owner, but the composite chain had omitted it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PKS — governed, machine-readable context for AI ... "context engineering" 2025–26
b_rows_sample.statement: PKS as governed, machine-readable AI context converges with industry 'context engineering' (Gartner July 2025: 'context engineering is in, prompt engineering is out', predicted in 80% of AI tools by 2028); enterprise practice defines governed, machine-readable context any AI agent can use reliably. b_rows_sample.anchor: The enforcement finding (governed context + advisory capabilities) ... 86% of enterprises are assembling rich, semantically grounded context — and handing it over with no governance
b_rows_sample.statement: The industry-wide finding that 86% of enterprises assemble rich context but hand it over with no governance over agent actions, and 89% say governance is critical while ~50% have it, is convergent with this platform's own governed-context-plus-advisory-capabilities gap.
