b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS generating a PKS (n=0) has only adjacent external support (context-engineering platforms generate context from metadata, not the same as generating a governed PKS); it remains a unique hypothesis needing operational proof only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
b_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concept relationships — the reviewer's example chain, validated ... KnowledgeOS creates PKS contains Engineering Knowledge organized by Ontology used by Capabilities executed through Runtime produces Evidence improves KnowledgeOS
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed chain is validated edge by edge: 'KnowledgeOS creates PKS' is a hypothesis (n=0, every PKS is authored by a person); 'PKS contains Engineering Knowledge' is WRONG, violating I-7 (a PKS contains product knowledge and bindings; reusable method must not live in it — the current breach is the exception that proves the rule); 'knowledge organized by Ontology' holds with the precision that L-A organizes artifacts/carriers, not knowledge itself (I-1); 'used by Capabilities' holds (capabilities may read across space boundaries, never own — H-1); 'Capabilities executed through Runtime' is imprecise (capabilities are advisory scripts invoked on demand; the runtime executes Execution Assets/ASTs; 41 enforced controls live runtime-side while every capability is advisory — the drawn edge hides this finding); 'Runtime produces Evidence' should attribute production to WORK (P-7/P-8), the runtime only hosts the work; 'Evidence improves KnowledgeOS' is only partly true (n≈3 informal, B-1's fact).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two corrections to the Addendum's own positioning ... "KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain" ... Contradicts a DA ruling
b_rows_sample.statement: Two corrections to an Addendum's positioning: (1) 'KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain' contradicts AIP-14/DA ruling 2026-07-27 that the Election System is the Core Domain and the platform is a Supporting Subdomain; the Reference Model records only the conditional (engineering knowledge would be Core Domain if the gate opened, and it has not). (2) 'PKS is a generated projection' was falsified last round: existing PKS artifacts carry Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS, a Commission, and ARB endorsement 9.9/10 — they are authored, not derived.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-3 · "PKS is a projection" — FALSIFIED for every existing PKS artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: The claim 'PKS is a projection' is falsified for every existing PKS artifact: examined fields (Authority: Generated, human-asserted; Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS; a Disposition History with ARB reviewer endorsement 9.9/10; a Commission) are incompatible with a projection, which would carry authority:derived (machine-checkable), no acceptance (regenerated, not accepted), a source and regeneration command, and no Commission. A mechanical grep for authority:derived|generated across docs/pks, docs/knowledgeos, docs/implementation returns 10 files, every one a prose mention of the vocabulary, not an application of it — those paths sit outside knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include. This sharpens a prior Ontology Classification finding ('blocked in practice') to stronger: existing PKS artifacts are positively authoritative — authored, commissioned, reviewed, disposed, and accepted — incompatible with 'derived'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-4 · D-7 "Context Type" was inferred from a single instance
b_rows_sample.statement: D-7's 'Context Type' claim (one PKS instance per product) was inferred from a single instance (PublicDigit's), with zero instances generated from the type; 'one instance per product' is an observation of one case restated as a rule — a type never instantiated is a description, not a discovered construct.

b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. a_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus says 'nobody ever asked'. ... Seven of eight are directly covered; the eighth is partial. The audit reported zero of five.
a_rows_sample.statement: A six-way Zero-lens dimension/value taxonomy (known / unknown Zero-A / not-assessed / absent / not-applicable / unresolved Zero-B) with five non-collapse laws (UNKNOWN!=ABSENT, UNRESOLVED!=INVALID, NOT_ASSESSED!=LOW_CONFIDENCE, NOT_APPLICABLE!=UNKNOWN, NO_EVIDENCE!=INVALID_EVIDENCE) plus a sixth boxed law (UnknownValue(D)!=UnknownDimension(D)), together with an independently-committed Abhava ontological absence typology (Pragabhava/Pradhvamsabhava/Atyantabhava/Anyonyabhava) and an AbsenceClaim record shape, jointly cover seven of the mandate's eight missingness cases directly and one partially -- versus the audit's report of zero of five covered.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is no component of K holding the set of recognised dimensions. ... D_t is the smallest missing component. With it, 'not assessed' is D in D_t AND not exists a in A: a.P.D=D -- decidable in O(n). Without it, the statement has no truth-maker.
a_rows_sample.statement: An executed probe (MISSINGNESS-NOT-ASSESSED in THEORY-CONSTRUCTION-TEST.md) shows a never-assessed dimension and an assessed-with-no-result dimension both render identically in K=(A,R) as 'no assertion mentioning that dimension', proving them provably indistinguishable; introducing D_t (the set of currently recognised dimensions) as a component of K makes 'not assessed' decidable in O(n) and is identified as the smallest missing component to close the missingness gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: VERIFIER RECOMMENDS -- not CORPUS ESTABLISHES. K = (D_t, A, R) ... with id = H(P, e_refs, c, t, Pi) where e_refs projects out the mutable state. ... Nothing here is adopted. This is a proposal, and it is smaller than the three the corpus already contains -- which should be consumed first (ES-005.4).
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes (explicitly labelled VERIFIER RECOMMENDS, not adopted) a minimal repair K=(D_t,A,R) adding the recognised-dimension set D_t and redefining id=H(P,e_refs,c,t,Pi) to project out the mutable state field, arguing this closes the missingness gap (7/8 cases), removes the identity/mutability contradiction, and makes a dedup operator definable by unioning Pi and e on (P,c,t); explicitly states this does not repair non-identifiability (needs a W,Omega layer beneath K) or uncertainty (needs U(H)), and that the corpus's own existing three constructions should be consumed first per ES-005.4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Empty != ContradictoryEvidence. ... Missing != False. ... EvalPolicy may need a third result: Undetermined.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues no-evidence must be distinguished from conflicting-evidence when assigning Sigma=Unknown, and that a missing required measurement (x=?) cannot be inferred as False; proposes a candidate three-valued policy-decision output {Permit, Deny, Undetermined} as a bridge between missingness and policy, explicitly marked as a candidate requiring corpus confirmation, not a final decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The three exclusions were a discovery failure, not a mathematical limit. They are absent from the AUTHORIZED MODEL v0.2 ... so the finding is real, and it is a GOVERNANCE finding: the constructions exist and were never promoted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a prior verdict ('THEORY CLOSED AGAINST THE STATED CRITERIA -- NOT COMPLETE IN EVERY RESPECT', with 'a theory that cannot say nobody ever asked is closed, not finished') by showing the corpus does say 'nobody ever asked' (the not-assessed Zero-lens dimension state, committed one day before this programme began) and does have formal, typed constructions for non-identifiability and uncertainty; reclassifies the three exclusions as a discovery failure rather than a mathematical limit, and as a governance finding since these constructions are measured absent (zero grep occurrences of unknown/absent/not assessed/uncertain/identifiab) from the authorized v0.2 model despite existing in the raw corpus.

a_rows_sample.anchor: - **`Missingness` — 0.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Three concepts have exactly zero definitional occurrences corpus-wide: Missingness (the concept exists richly under other names — Zero, abhāva, Missing, 'not assessed' — so this is a vocabulary gap masquerading as a theory gap), Admissibility (its two laws are cited constantly, 42.9/42.41, but the term itself is never defined), and AuthorityAct (confirming, by whole-corpus scan rather than targeted grep, that the object the entire governance model turns on has no type).

a_rows_sample.statement: 8 of 9 mandated missingness distinctions (not-asked, asked-but-no-answer, unknown, absent, no-evidence-found, searched-but-insufficient, deliberately-omitted, deleted; only 'never existed'/Prāgabhāva lacks one) have a named corpus construct across the Zero taxonomy and the Sanskrit abhāva typology, and 4 of them (unknown, absent, insufficient, not-applicable) are executable, tested, passing code in zero_reference.py (8/8 tests); the word 'Missingness' itself has 0 definitional occurrences, so searching for the word finds nothing while the capability exists richly under other names.

a_rows_sample.anchor: With D_t: "not assessed" is D ∈ D_t ∧ ¬∃a ∈ 𝒜 : a.P.D = D — decidable in O(n).
a_rows_sample.statement: The Zero model's D_t (recognised-dimension set) plus Z_t=Omega\Represented(K_t) layer, already present in the corpus, makes 'not assessed' a decidable O(n) predicate (D in D_t and no assertion covers D), and this is proposed as the minimum additional structural component needed -- not invented, but recovered from the corpus's own Zero-lens construction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown is expressible neither as a value nor as an absence. It must be a sigma, and sigma is not in A in the terminal type ... Unknown currently has nowhere to live.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding CS-5: (Nexus,version,UNKNOWN) puts an epistemic marker in the value space, the exact category error Step 264 (264.11, 264.13) warns against; treating Unknown as assertion-absence is indistinguishable from never-having-asked, destroying the Zero concept's asked-vs-never-asked distinction (025d); since sigma is not a field of the terminal A=(id,P,e,c,t,Pi), Unknown has no representational home in either direction.

Note: A ten-point falsification checklist (T1-T10) derived directly from the classical Nyaya logic textbook Tarka-sangraha/Dipika in S0398 (lakshana definition-defects, five-member inference, vyapti/anvaya/vyatireka, hetvabhasa fallacies, samsaya, viparyaya, abhava/pratiyogi, nigrahasthana), explicitly scoped as an argument-validity lens distinct from the Williamson epistemic-status lens.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Nyaya treats knowledge as fundamentally relational and process-based, not as a static property of propositions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Three headline findings from applying Nyaya pramana theory, tarka, realism, and debate theory to the Kernel: (1) knowledge is relational/process-based, not a static property -- a claim is knowledge only if generated by the right kind of process (pramana) and defeasible by legitimate doubt; (2) Nyaya's two-tier epistemology (default trust in cognition vs reflective certification when doubt arises) maps onto a 'knowledge core' (trusted default) vs 'adjudication process' (certification) distinction; (3) Nyaya's theory of error is parasitic on truth (error is misplacement of properties onto the wrong object, requiring prior knowledge of the properties/object), directly relevant to the anti-reasoner concept and the representation-!=-truth problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Requires Four Factors
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten Nyaya observations (Part 1): (1) knowledge requires four unified factors -- knower, known, knowledge source, and knowledge itself (Nyaya-sutra 1.1.1); (2) error is parasitic on truth, a misplacement of a property onto the wrong object (Nyaya-sutra 4.2.35, the shell/silver example); (3) a two-tier epistemology of default trust vs certification when doubt arises (2.1.20); (4) pramanas (perception/inference/analogy/testimony, 1.1.3) are causes of veridical cognition, not conscious justifications -- a causal account of knowledge; (5) inference (linga) has a three-part perception->recollection->inference structure (1.1.5); (6) vyapti (invariable concomitance) must be tested in both anvaya (positive) and vyatireka (negative) directions (1.1.34); (7) absence (abhava) requires a counter-correlative (pratiyogi), you cannot assert non-existence of X without knowing what X would be if it existed (4.2.33); (8) perception is defined by four conditions (sense-object connection, language-independence, inerrancy, definitiveness, 1.1.4); (9) the lamp analogy is interpreted as mutual certification among pramanas, not self-certification (2.1.19), a coherentist element within Nyaya's foundationalism; (10) doubt (samsaya) is the catalyst for inquiry, not a failure state, arising from five distinct triggers (1.1.23).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The 10 Strongest Falsification Questions from Nyaya
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten falsification questions mirroring the ten observations: definition adequacy (avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava, and whether 'does not depend on language' is even met by a digital system); reason integrity via the five-part pratijna-hetu-udaharana-upanaya-nigamana structure; invariant testing in both anvaya/vyatireka directions; absence-type question for 'retraction'; the five hetvabhasa (pseudo-prover) defects (deviant/contradictory/inconclusive/unproven/mistimed); representation vs truth (viparyaya); whether unknown/doubt/contradiction/error are collapsed into one 'uncertain' state (samsaya); conclusion-excess (nigamana exceeding pratijna+hetu); nigrahasthana argument-integrity checks (proposition/reason changed, meaning shifted); and whether the Kernel distinguishes knowledge by pramana source.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is a Causal Process, Not a Property
a_rows_sample.statement: Five most-surprising observations: knowledge is generated by a causal process, not possessed as a property (a Kernel might need to track the generation process/pramana, not just the claim); error requires prior knowledge of truth (opposite of the Western default-doubt assumption, so error might be modeled as a modified version of truth, not a separate category); default trust, not skepticism, is Nyaya's epistemic starting point (opposite of the Cartesian default-doubt assumption); absence is a real category with structure (counter-correlative plus type: absolute/prior/subsequent/locus-based); doubt has five distinct causal types, not just confidence degrees.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The 5 Observations Most Likely Relevant to a Minimal Knowledge Kernel
a_rows_sample.statement: Five observations ranked most kernel-relevant: the four-factor knower/known/source/knowledge relational structure (a Kernel storing only propositions loses this structure); the two-tier trusted-vs-certified structure; the parasitism thesis (error as modified truth, not a separate category); the counter-correlative requirement for absence/retraction/deletion; the five distinct doubt types (not just a confidence scalar).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Debate Framework as Falsification Apparatus
a_rows_sample.statement: Nyaya's three debate types (vada: truth-seeking debate using pramanas/tarka without tricks; jalpa: disputation using equivocation/misleading objections/clinchers; vitanda: destructive debate refuting without establishing) plus the five-component formal demonstration (proposition/reason/illustration/application/conclusion), five pseudo-provers, and twenty-two clinchers (ways to lose an argument) suggest a Kernel 'argument integrity' test checking definitional defects (avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava), reason defects (savyabhicara/viruddha/satpratipaksa/asiddha/badhita), and argument integrity (proposition/reason/meaning changes).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 5 Observations That Should NOT Influence Architecture Without Further Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Five Nyaya observations explicitly flagged as not (yet) architecturally actionable: perception-as-inerrant (too specific an epistemological claim); the four metaphysical categories (substance/quality/action/universal); Nyaya's theism (God as causal factor, not relevant to a minimal kernel); the full 22-clincher list (more detail than a minimal kernel needs); Nyaya's realism about universals (jati) as a specific ontological claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Questions That Conventional DDD Analysis May Not Expose
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten DDD-blind-spot questions: relational (knower/known/source/knowledge) vs identity-holder aggregates; causal generation vs internal justification; error-as-modified-truth vs error-as-separate-category; absence-requires-counter-correlative vs absence-as-non-existence; five doubt types vs a degree-of-uncertainty scalar; knowledge-as-generated-by-causes vs knowledge-as-possession; perception-as-inerrant-by-definition vs perception-as-fallible; testimony-as-inerrant-when-trustworthy vs testimony-as-fallible; definitions tested for avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava vs definition-as-neutral-act; multi-stage (perception/recollection/reflection) vs linear inference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: These are not questions about missing capabilities. They are questions about the assumptions the Kernel makes about the nature of knowledge itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final consolidated ten architect-facing questions restating the Part 1-2 material: default-trust vs mandatory-certification; error as separate category vs modified truth; knowledge as static property vs dynamic knower/known/source/knowledge relationship; absence types requiring a counter-correlative; five doubt types vs a single uncertainty state; self-testing definitions for avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava; distinguishing the generation process (pramana) from the knowledge itself; representing that generation process per unit of knowledge; self-certifying vs mutually-certifying knowledge sources; retraction as discrete deletion vs gradual correction process.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is not merely a claim. Knowledge is the result of a disciplined process involving a knower, an object, a means of knowing, conditions of validity, possible error, and—when challenged—a structured process of reasoning and verification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extraction from Arthur Berriedale Keith's Indian Logic and Atomism: An Exposition of the Nyaya and Vaicesika Systems (1921), valued not for Vaisheshika atomism but for the Nyaya theory of knowledge/proof/inference/error/debate/categories/relations; central discovery: knowledge is a disciplined process involving a knower, an object, a means of knowing, conditions of validity, possible error, and (when challenged) structured reasoning/verification, modeled as Reality/Object->Knowledge<-Means of Knowing<-{Perception,Inference,Testimony}->Cognition->{True->Verified, False->Error}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-001 ... cognizer, cognition, cognized ... KOS-NYAYA-002 ... knowledge ≠ valid knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-001: distinguish the knower, knowing, and known (cognizer/cognition/cognized) -- KnowledgeClaim must never be collapsed with KnowledgeEvent, KnowledgeSubject, or KnowledgeObject, proposing KnowledgeSubject-performs->KnowledgeProcess-produces->Cognition-about->KnowledgeObject. KOS-NYAYA-002 (rated the single most important extraction): knowledge has a validity dimension -- a genuine pramana (means of proof) must produce true knowledge agreeing with reality, so knowledge!=valid knowledge and information!=knowledge; proposes KnowledgeAssertion{proposition, epistemic_basis, validity_status, scope, provenance}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-003 ... source ≠ method ≠ result ... KOS-NYAYA-004 ... KOS-NYAYA-005 ... Validity is externally challengeable
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-003: a means of knowledge is defined by the knowledge it produces -- pramana is a mode/process, not a static instrument, giving Evidence+Process+Conditions=Epistemic Basis and source!=method!=result (a Database is not itself knowledge, a Query is not itself knowledge, a Query result is not automatically knowledge; chain source->method->observation->cognition->claim). KOS-NYAYA-004: validity requires agreement with reality (truth as cognition-object correspondence), distinguishing representation from truth claim from world/evidence correspondence. KOS-NYAYA-005: validity is externally challengeable -- cognition is not automatically valid merely by occurring, but established through verification and revisable by further evidence or defects, proposing ValidityStatus{proposed, supported, accepted, challenged, invalidated, superseded} -- 'knowledge must be revisable', 'valid' does not mean 'eternally valid.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-006 ... Error is not the same as the cognition event ... Negative and superseded knowledge are still knowledge about the evolution of the knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-006: error is not the same as the cognition event -- the shell/silver mistaking example shows the wrongness lies in the result/interpretation, not the cognitive occurrence itself, so FalseClaim!=NoKnowledge; a mistaken claim (Observation->Cognition->Interpretation->Claim->later correction) remains historically important epistemic evidence, converging with Williamson's revision/deletion distinction: 'negative and superseded knowledge are still knowledge about the evolution of the knowledge state.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-007 ... A knowledge claim should declare how it is known.
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-007: knowledge has multiple legitimate epistemic routes (perception, inference, comparison, verbal testimony -- with historical disagreement among schools about which count as independent), giving a proposed EpistemicBasis{Observation, Inference, Analogy/Comparison, Testimony, ...} explicitly not hard-coded to four categories; deeper principle: 'a knowledge claim should declare how it is known.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-008 ... vyapti — invariable concomitance ... KOS-NYAYA-009 ... Positive evidence AND absence of contrary evidence matter
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-008: inference requires a stable relation (vyapti, invariable concomitance between reason and consequence), not merely repeated observation -- the classic smoke->fire pattern relies on an established invariant relation, not a mere co-occurrence tally. KOS-NYAYA-009 (rated a major five-star KOS principle, called one of the most valuable parts for assurance architecture): positive evidence AND absence of contrary evidence both matter -- observing concomitance in a few cases is insufficient; a suspected discrepancy must be explained as apparent or force the relation to be treated as conditional, so KnowledgeOS should store EvidenceAgainst/Counterexample/BoundaryCondition alongside EvidenceFor, structured as Hypothesis H{positive instances, negative instances, contrary cases, boundary conditions}->invariant?

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-010 ... KOS-NYAYA-011 ... mere juxtaposition of propositions does not produce the inference
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-010: a suspected exception is epistemically significant -- an agent should maintain Rule R alongside evidence supporting it, known exceptions, suspected exceptions, and scope conditions, proposing Invariant{proposition, supporting_cases, contrary_cases, scope, conditions, status}. KOS-NYAYA-011 (rated a major AI Engineering principle): inference is not just mechanical premise assembly -- Nyaya explicitly rejects mere juxtaposition of propositions as sufficient for inference (premises must combine through a genuine mental/inferential operation), so retrieved-facts+retrieved-facts does not automatically equal reasoning; proposes Premises->Relation Recognition->Inference Operation->Conclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-012 ... inference for oneself vs inference for another ... KOS-NYAYA-013 ... five-member Nyaya syllogism
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-012: distinguish private reasoning from communicated reasoning -- 'inference for oneself' vs 'inference for another' (a structured exposition letting a hearer reproduce the reasoning), giving InternalInference != Justification, so an agent's internally-reached conclusion C still requires an externally-reproducible 'why C?' -- a major connection to deterministic AI assurance. KOS-NYAYA-013: a justification should expose the inferential structure -- the five-member syllogism (proposition/reason/example-concomitance/application/conclusion, where the example explains why the reason suffices) proposes a Justification{claim, reason, governing_relation, evidence, application, conclusion} object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-014 ... examples can function as semantic/epistemic bridges ... KOS-NYAYA-015 ... KOS-NYAYA-016 ... deficiency (nyuna) ... redundancy (adhika)
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-014: examples can function as semantic/epistemic bridges (General Principle->Example->Concrete Case), likened to Architecture Principle->Reference Example->Current Implementation. KOS-NYAYA-015: logical errors deserve first-class modeling (fallacious/unproved/doubtful reasons stem from failed invariable concomitance), proposing ArgumentEvaluation{valid, unsupported, contradictory, ambiguous, insufficient, circular, scope_violation, other} rather than a binary valid/invalid, with categories to be derived systematically rather than adopted wholesale from this source. KOS-NYAYA-016: deficiency (nyuna) and redundancy (adhika) and tenet-deviation are distinct failure modes, mapped to a missing governing assumption in an ADR, duplicated authority across three locations, and an implementation violating an accepted principle respectively -- 'argument and architecture failures can be classified structurally rather than merely labeled wrong.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-017 ... Criticism must respect the opponent's accepted premises ... strongly reinforces the Williamson extraction about neutral semantic mappings
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-017 (rated a five-star cross-source convergence): criticism must respect the opponent's accepted premises -- one cannot criticize a Buddhist school for not using the Nyaya five-member syllogism if it recognizes a different structure; applied to evaluating an external bounded context or architecture: do not impose our vocabulary and declare theirs invalid, instead understand its own rules, evaluate internally, map to our model, then compare -- explicitly reinforcing Williamson's neutral-semantic-mapping extraction (S0436).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-018 ... Truth-seeking debate is different from adversarial victory ... KOS-NYAYA-019 ... KOS-NYAYA-020 ... KOS-NYAYA-021 ... Hypothetical adoption
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-018/019: truth-seeking debate (Question->Clarification->Evidence->Reason->Counterargument->Resolution) is distinguished from victory-oriented debate (fraud/futile-objections/cavilling/wrangling: Goal=win->select evidence->attack opponent->move goalposts->produce rhetoric), suggesting an AI agent needs an explicit epistemic objective (establish_best_supported_claim, not defend_current_proposal) -- recommended for the AI Engineering Platform governance methodology. KOS-NYAYA-020: accepted assumptions should be explicit -- shared/related-school/derived/provisional (hypothetical) premise categories give SharedPremise/LocalPremise/DerivedPremise/HypotheticalPremise. KOS-NYAYA-021: hypothetical adoption is a legitimate reasoning technique -- temporarily accepting an opponent's view without endorsing it, deriving consequences to find contradictions, corresponding to 'architecture counterfactual analysis' (Assume Architecture A->derive consequences->identify contradiction/limitation), proposing HypotheticalArgument{assumed_position, assumption_scope, derived_consequences, contradiction, conclusion}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-022 ... samavaya — inherence ... KOS-NYAYA-023 ... Relationship types deserve ontological status
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-022: ontology requires categories AND relations -- Vaisheshika's seven categories (Substance/Quality/Activity/Generality/Particularity/Inherence/Non-existence) are not themselves to be adopted, but the key insight is that an ontology needs both entities and the relations explaining how entities belong together, especially samavaya (inherence, a relation between things that cannot exist separately, substrate/inhere). KOS-NYAYA-023 (rated a five-star ontology research candidate): relationship types deserve ontological status -- software architecture often models entities but leaves relations as unexamined arrows; implements/depends-on/supports/contradicts/realizes/contains/belongs-to/instantiates are not interchangeable, and Nyaya-Vaisesika forces the question 'what kind of relation is this?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-024 ... KOS-NYAYA-025 ... Generality and particularity must coexist ... Never confuse the class/type/generalization with the concrete knowledge instance.
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-024: don't collapse 'part-of', 'property-of', and 'relation-to' -- Entity/Property/Activity/Relation must remain distinguishable (Aggregate is not the same type of thing as AggregateState, and neither is depends-on), reinforcing DDD modeling discipline. KOS-NYAYA-025: generality and particularity must coexist (Domain Concept->{general concept, particular instance}), illustrated by ArchitectureDecision vs ADR-T19, or Evidence vs TestRun-2026-08-24-001; candidate principle: 'never confuse the class/type/generalization with the concrete knowledge instance.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-026 ... abhava — non-existence/negation ... KOS-NYAYA-027 ... Absence is relational
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-026: non-existence/absence can be knowledge -- later Vaisheshika recognizes abhava (non-existence/negation) as a category with multiple forms and explicit relations to what is absent; 'no evidence found', 'capability absent', 'architecture boundary violated', 'expected artifact missing', 'entity no longer exists' are knowledge about absence, not merely empty values. KOS-NYAYA-027: absence is relational -- non-existence is connected to a positive counterpart and substrate, so 'Missing(X)' is incomplete; proposes AbsenceAssertion{expected_object, observed_scope, expectation_source, observation_time, evidence}, e.g. Missing(ArchitectureDecision) requiring these fields to be a proper knowledge object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-028 ... KOS-NYAYA-029 ... Ontological simplicity can hide causal complexity ... Do not choose an ontology merely because it is elegant if it cannot represent important real-world causal structures.
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-028: causality needs explicit structure -- Keith identifies weaknesses in the Nyaya-Vaisesika causal theory's treatment of multiple/complex causes, used as a warning (not an endorsement of their theory) that a simple A->B causal model can fail when reality has interacting causes, requiring distinct necessary-cause/contributing-cause/trigger/enabling-condition/instrument/context relations. KOS-NYAYA-029 (a researcher inference from the author's own criticism, explicitly not a direct Nyaya principle): ontological simplicity can hide causal complexity -- 'do not choose an ontology merely because it is elegant if it cannot represent important real-world causal structures', connecting directly to Williamson's warning that simplicity is not merely minimum entity count.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-030 ... KOS-NYAYA-031 ... Knowledge has a history ... KOS-NYAYA-032 ... A formal system can contain unresolved historical uncertainty
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-030/031: the system evolved through criticism and synthesis (initial formulations->commentaries->criticism->Buddhist interaction->internal revision->syncretism->later refinement, with aphoristic sutras requiring commentary and functioning partly as mnemonic structures) -- a knowledge system should preserve original claim->interpretation->criticism->revision->current formulation rather than flattening into one canonical truth, proposing KnowledgeObject{current_version, predecessors, successors, interpretations, criticisms, supersession}. KOS-NYAYA-032: a formal system can contain unresolved historical uncertainty -- Keith explicitly warns dates/origins/interpretations are uncertain and absolutely certain results cannot always be achieved, so KnowledgeOS should represent Known/Probable/Contested/Uncertain/Reconstructed/Unknown rather than forcing binary true/false.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-033 ... Provenance matters ... KOS-NYAYA-034 ... A source's authority is itself a knowledge problem ... KOS-NYAYA-035 ... testimony and inference should remain distinct epistemic paths
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-033: provenance matters -- the same proposition can have different provenance (original text/commentary/later interpretation/historical reconstruction), giving Claim{source, author, historical layer, interpretation, reconstruction status}. KOS-NYAYA-034: a source's authority is itself a knowledge problem -- historical disagreement over whether verbal testimony is an independent means of knowledge or reducible to inference; 'Source says X' must never automatically mean 'X is true', requiring Source->Testimony->Authority evaluation->Knowledge claim, proposing TestimonialEvidence{speaker, statement, authority_basis, reliability, scope, corroboration}. KOS-NYAYA-035: testimony and inference should remain distinct epistemic paths even when they support the same claim (observed X / inferred X / told X by an authority / compared X with Y are not interchangeable justifications).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-NYAYA-036 ... KOS-NYAYA-037 ... A claim can have multiple independent supports ... KOS-NYAYA-038 ... Epistemic relations are not all equivalent
b_rows_sample.statement: KOS-NYAYA-036: epistemic basis should survive representation -- a claim like 'Capability X exists' should preserve whether its basis is an architecture document, source-code inspection, runtime observation, or expert testimony. KOS-NYAYA-037: a claim can have multiple independent supports simultaneously (Claim C supported-by Evidence E1, supported-by Inference I1, corroborated-by Test T1, confirmed-by Observation O1), stronger than a single claim.source field. KOS-NYAYA-038: epistemic relations are not all equivalent -- argues against a generic 'supports' relation, proposing observes/infers/testifies/compares/corroborates/contradicts/invalidates/presupposes/derives/applies as a major candidate for a formal ontology.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Nyaya provides conceptual structures that are highly compatible with disciplined domain modeling ... candidate bounded context: Epistemology
b_rows_sample.statement: A full DDD translation of the extraction (explicitly not claiming 'Nyaya is DDD', only that it 'provides conceptual structures highly compatible with disciplined domain modeling'): candidate bounded context Epistemology with aggregates KnowledgeClaim/Inference/Evidence/Argument/Cognition/Validation/Dispute; value objects EpistemicBasis/ValidityStatus/Scope/Assumption/Counterexample/Provenance; domain events ClaimProposed/EvidenceObserved/InferenceConstructed/ClaimChallenged/CounterexampleFound/ClaimValidated/ClaimInvalidated/ClaimSuperseded; a key insight maps Nyaya's general-relation vs particular-application distinction directly onto Domain invariant -> Concrete aggregate instance (example: 'a determination must be issued only after persistence' -> 'Determination #123 was persisted, therefore DeterminationIssued is valid').

b_rows_sample.anchor: a Nyaya-inspired epistemic checklist ... but adapted to engineering
b_rows_sample.statement: Two applied structures proposed: (1) a Nyaya-inspired ten-question AI-agent investigation checklist (what is the proposition? what is the object under investigation? what is the evidence? what is the epistemic basis? what general relation is relied upon? what assumptions are made? are there contrary cases? can the conclusion be independently reproduced? what logical errors are possible? what would invalidate the conclusion?), replacing a bare 'what is the architecture?' query; (2) an architecture-review artifact structured as Proposition->Reason->General Relation->Evidence{positive cases, negative cases, counterexamples}->Application->Conclusion, judged more rigorous than an ordinary prose ADR.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge claims must be traceable to their generation process ... Error is a modified version of truth, not a distinct state ... Default trust is the epistemic default ... trust by default and doubt only on reason.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traceable Generation pattern (Nyaya pramana): every knowledge unit records its source/generation conditions; error is modeled as a misplacement rather than a distinct category; the epistemic default is trust, with doubt requiring a reason.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `EvidenceLinks` (l. 209) carries *"evidence references + **acquisition method** + reliability conditions."* **Acquisition method is already there.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Session 1 claims three separate carriers an evidence/claim reference may need: route (S1-F035, by what epistemic means was this obtained, e.g. pratyaksa vs upamana), acquisition procedure (S1-F030), and role (S1-F029). This review disputes the count: EvidenceLinks (l.209) already carries evidence references plus acquisition method plus reliability conditions -- acquisition method is already in law -- and route is very close to acquisition method, so whether they are one carrier or two is the same semantic-denotation question left open at two prior reviews (S2-R-F029, S2-R-F030). The defensible composite is smaller: one carrier already in law (acquisition/route, possibly one thing) plus one genuinely absent carrier (role).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Tarka is a kind of conjectural reasoning (uha)... Tarka is NOT an independent pramana... It is 'Pramana-anugrahaka' — an assistant to the pramanas.
b_rows_sample.statement: Cites Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy definitions of tarka as conjectural reasoning that reveals a thing's real nature by showing the absurdity of contrary characters, and as explicitly not an independent pramana but an assistant to the pramanas (does not itself produce definitive cognition; functions as reductio ad absurdum / prasanga).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Five Types of Tarka (Fallacious Structures to Avoid): Pramanabadhita, Atmasraya, Anyonyasraya, Cakrakasraya, Anavastha
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists tarka's function as reductio ad absurdum with a worked example (self as eternal vs produced, via karmic-inheritance absurdity), and enumerates five fallacious-tarka structures to avoid: contradicted-by-valid-knowledge, self-dependency, mutual dependency, circular dependency, infinite regress.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status: Apramana (not a knowledge source) vs Pramana (valid knowledge source) ... Function: Tests competing claims, removes doubt vs Derives new knowledge from evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Full comparison table of Tarka vs Anumana across status (apramana/pramana), function (tests vs derives), independence (assistant vs independent source), outcome (eliminates alternatives/confirms vyapti vs produces valid inference), and worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: reason (tarka) must serve scripture (sruti), not replace it ... Dustarkat suviramyatam — Srutimatas tarko'nusandhiyatam ... Should KnowledgeOS reasoning be constrained by organizational authority? The Vedic model suggests: Yes
b_rows_sample.statement: Cites Sankaracarya's warning against dustarka (corrupt/futile reasoning contrary to authority) and Nyaya's self-conception as a rational defender of Hindu religious culture, then argues this raises the architectural question of whether KnowledgeOS reasoning should be constrained by organizational authority, answering 'Yes' by analogy, aligning with Evidence != Authority / Assessment != Authority.

b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate invariant TARKA-003: reasoning that tests claims (tarka) is distinct from reasoning that produces knowledge (anumana); classified 'strong candidate'.

b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate invariant TARKA-005: reasoning must respect organizational authority boundaries (no dustarka); classified 'strong candidate', said to reinforce existing governance principles.

b_rows_sample.statement: Final discipline statement: distinguishes what external research establishes (what is known in the field) from what EKS/PKS/AIP archaeology establishes (what KnowledgeOS actually has); only their comparison can determine relevance; the document explicitly bars itself from designing the kernel, choosing technology, defining bounded contexts, creating ADRs, or proposing migration, self-classifying as 'NOT ARCHITECTURE EVIDENCE / NO KERNEL DECISION'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lakṣaṇa — definition adequacy ... Vyāpti — the hidden invariant test ... Hetvābhāsa — attack the reason itself ... Saṃśaya — don't collapse unresolved alternatives ... Abhāva — absence needs a counter-correlate ... Nigrahasthāna — identify where an argument has actually failed
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives a nine-family falsification instrument from the Tarka-sangraha (with Dipika commentary), explicitly as an instrument rather than a source of content: (1) Laksana definition adequacy, (2) Paksa-Sadhya-Hetu discipline (claim/thing-to-prove/reason kept distinct), (3) Vyapti hidden-invariant test (is the claimed universal relation actually universal), (4) Hetvabhasa (fallacy classes in the reason), (5) Samsaya (do not collapse unresolved alternatives prematurely), (6) Viparyaya (erroneous apprehension/misattribution), (7) Abhava (unqualified negative claims need a counter-correlate), (8) Anvaya-Vyatireka (one-sided causal inference), (9) Nigrahasthana (identify where an argument has actually failed); operationalizes family 1 directly as 'does our definition of the Kernel have avyapti (under-inclusion), ativyapti (over-inclusion), or asambhava (impossibility under the Constitution)?'.

=> Of 10 propositions the corpus itself requires, 2 are cleanly expressible.
     THREE are inexpressible
a_rows_sample.statement: EXP-19: tested against 10 propositions the corpus itself states it needs to express, P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) cleanly expresses only 2; 3 are inexpressible (negation — no negative values in V_D; conditional — 'IF v>=3.60 THEN patch-current', the founding conditional-determination problem; universal quantification — 'every committee has >=3 members'); 2 are lossy (a validity interval collapses to one timestamp t; a unit is dropped); 1 ('A1 contradicts A2') is not a proposition at all in this type system and must be expressed as an R-edge instead, giving the theory two uncoordinated mechanisms for propositional content; 1 ('Nexus is ready to migrate') is expressible but empty, holding the conclusion with no way to express the rule that produced it; 1 ('Nexus.version is UNKNOWN') is ambiguous between a value-space category error and true absence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I read the attached document in full. My assessment is that it is useful, but it is not yet safe to merge into the KnowledgeOS theory as written ... The most important work is therefore not to add all 10 proposed distinctions. It is to extract the valid theoretical contribution, correct the formalism, and prevent R_req from becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Executive verdict on an R_req/ratification-style document: classified as research analysis / candidate specification, not yet ratifiable; explicitly rejects the document's own recommendation to add all ten proposed distinctions and to ratify, warning against R_req becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology'; distills the strongest contribution as R_req = the distinctions that must remain available for KnowledgeOS's required questions, combined with Representation Adequacy iff required distinctions are preserved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the stronger KnowledgeOS definition should be: Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R preserves all distinctions in D_Q(Gamma) ... not: R preserves every distinction in D. The document itself notices this problem under projection adequacy, where it recommends allowing lower-tier distinctions to be lost. That observation should actually be moved up into the fundamental definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the pairwise-preservation definition of adequacy (d(x)!=d(y) implies R(x)!=R(y) for all d) to be question-relative from the start: Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R preserves all distinctions in D_Q(Gamma), not all distinctions in D universally -- because a representation may legitimately collapse a distinction irrelevant to the current question; promotes an observation the original document made only under 'projection adequacy' up into the foundational definition.

type_signature.domain: representation R, question Q, context Gamma

a_rows_sample.anchor: For KnowledgeOS: Required != Interesting != Available in literature. A distinction belongs in R_req only if we can establish that some KnowledgeOS question, invariant, operation, assurance requirement or boundary requires it. ... analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent, intentional/extensional, de dicto/de re ... their existence in the KR/philosophy literature does not establish that KnowledgeOS must preserve them.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the principle Required != Interesting != Available-in-literature: a distinction enters R_req only if some KnowledgeOS question, invariant, operation, assurance requirement, or boundary can be shown to require it; existence in KR/philosophy literature alone (cited for analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent, intensional/extensional, de dicto/de re) is not sufficient grounds.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. Strong candidates: 1. Truth vs. validity ... 2. Satisfiability vs. unsatisfiability ... 3. Soundness vs. completeness ... 4. Decidability vs. undecidability ... 5. Local vs. global scope ... 6. Intensional vs. extensional ... 7. De dicto vs. de re ... B. Probably outside core R_req: Analytic vs. synthetic ... A priori vs. a posteriori ... Necessary vs. contingent ... These should remain external research candidates, not Tier 2 requirements.
a_rows_sample.statement: Splits the document's ten proposed additional distinctions into Group A (strong candidates deserving further KnowledgeOS work: truth-vs-validity, satisfiability-vs-unsatisfiability, soundness-vs-completeness, decidability-vs-undecidability, local-vs-global scope, intensional-vs-extensional, de-dicto-vs-de-re) and Group B (probably outside core R_req: analytic-vs-synthetic, a-priori-vs-a-posteriori, necessary-vs-contingent), recommending Group B remain external research candidates rather than Tier 2 requirements.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth vs. Validity -- |=alpha vs. Sigma|=alpha. This is not a clean distinction ... So the important distinction is: Validity != Entailment rather than: Truth != Validity. At the semantic level: M|=alpha is truth of alpha in a model M. Then |=alpha is validity across all models. And Sigma|=alpha is entailment from Sigma. This should be corrected before incorporating the item.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a formal error in the source document's Truth-vs-Validity distinction: the real three-way distinction is M|=alpha (truth of alpha in model M) versus |=alpha (validity: true in every model) versus Sigma|=alpha (entailment from Sigma); the document's proposed 'Truth vs Validity' pairing is not clean and should be replaced by Validity != Entailment before incorporation.

type_signature.domain: formula alpha, model M, theory Sigma

a_rows_sample.anchor: we already have a critical KnowledgeOS boundary: Satisfiability != Contr because satisfiability is relative to Semantics + Language + ModelClass. Thus: Cons_S(K) iff exists M, M |=_S K could be a candidate formal consistency property. But it must not become: Contr(K) = not Cons_S(K). ... The attached document itself later says Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status. That is actually evidence against identifying Contr with ordinary satisfiability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects identifying Contr with ordinary model-theoretic satisfiability: Satisfiability != Contr, since satisfiability is relative to Semantics+Language+ModelClass; proposes Cons_S(K) iff exists M: M|=_S K as a candidate formal consistency property distinct from Contr(K)=not-Cons_S(K), citing the source document's own admission that Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status as evidence against the satisfiability identification, and listing Contr's broader required distinctions (genuine contradiction, incompatible contexts, temporal divergence, supersession, insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness).

type_signature.domain: knowledge base K under reasoning system S

a_rows_sample.anchor: soundness and completeness are properties of a reasoning system: Sound(S), Complete(S,Q). They are not properties of Knowledge itself. This should therefore be added under: Formal Representation and Reasoning rather than as a universal epistemic distinction. ... Decidability is a property of a problem/procedure/formal system ... Decidable(S,Q) ... Therefore: Decidability != EpistemicStatus. But it is extremely valuable as a reasoning-system capability/property. This fits our existing Complexity(S,Q) work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies Soundness (Sound(S)), Completeness (Complete(S,Q)), and Decidability (Decidable(S,Q)) as properties of the reasoning system S (a problem/procedure/formal-system property), not properties of Knowledge itself and not epistemic distinctions (Decidability != EpistemicStatus, distinct from Known(p) and Determined(p)); recommends filing them under 'Formal Representation and Reasoning' alongside an existing Complexity(S,Q) line of work rather than as universal epistemic distinctions in R_req.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document identifies a weakness in its own preservation criterion: it does not account for context-sensitivity. This is correct. I would make the correction stronger. Instead of D_Q we should eventually have D_Q(Gamma) ... R_req may be a global baseline, while the actual required distinction set is: R_req(Q,Gamma). This is a major improvement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the source document's own context-sensitivity self-correction: replaces D_Q with D_Q(Gamma) where Gamma bundles context, scope, time, authority, task, and representation regime; correspondingly R_req becomes a global baseline while the actually-applicable set is R_req(Q,Gamma) -- described as a major theoretical improvement over a fixed universal set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I disagree with 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' ... A Tier-1 distinction d3 could be irrelevant to that question. Then R_1 may legitimately discard d3. So Tier(d) should influence governance priority, but should not automatically determine semantic preservation. The better rule is: Requiredness(Q,Gamma) > Tier.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the rule 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' as too rigid: even a Tier-1 distinction may be legitimately discarded by a representation used only for a task whose D_Q does not require it. Proposes Tier should govern governance priority, not automatically determine semantic preservation, i.e. Requiredness(Q,Gamma) takes precedence over Tier.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document says transformation invariance should preserve distinctions, but then recognizes that transformations may intentionally modify distinctions ... define a transformation's declared change set: Chg(T) subseteq R. Then: d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d. This is much better for KnowledgeOS because some operations are supposed to change state. Otherwise the preservation requirement makes state transition impossible.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the transformation-invariance rule: instead of requiring T to preserve all of R_req, defines a declared change set Chg(T) subseteq R such that d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d; explicitly noting that an unconditional preservation requirement would make state transition impossible, since some operations are supposed to change state.

type_signature.domain: transformation T and distinction set R
type_signature.codomain: Chg(T) subseteq R, plus a preservation obligation on R minus Chg(T)

a_rows_sample.anchor: The document says: delta must preserve all R_req distinctions. I would explicitly reject this formulation ... What must be preserved are the invariants declared applicable to that transition. So: InvariantCustody(delta) is preferable to: PreserveAll(delta, R_req). This aligns directly with our existing invariant-custody research.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects the claim 'delta must preserve all R_req distinctions': a transition delta(K_t,a)->K_{t+1} may intentionally change status, support, currency, resolution, scope, even representation; proposes InvariantCustody(delta) -- preserving only the invariants declared applicable to that specific transition -- as preferable to PreserveAll(delta,R_req), aligned with existing invariant-custody research.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Zero requires all Tier 1 distinctions' should NOT be adopted ... Zero does not necessarily need every distinction in R_req. Instead: Zero(K,I,Gamma,L) asks what is not justified by the available representation within the declared inquiry boundary. b_rows_sample.anchor: Model B executed -- K=(C,sigma,theta,lambda) with policy as an argument to T ... If pi in K, then revoking or amending a policy changes every stored state, while nothing that is known has changed. ... VERDICT: pi is EXTERNAL. MATHEMATICALLY VERIFIED by counterexample.

Verdict: pi is external to K, mathematically verified.

Verdict: History(K)!=K is fundamental; lambda belongs outside K as History:K->Histories, mathematically verified, and aligned with the real implementation (a separate lineage graph, no KnowledgeState).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We want to know whether there exists a corresponding state transformation T:K x I -> K such that F(That(H,i)) = T(F(H),i) for every valid H and input i. If this holds, then the history dynamics descend to the state space.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sets up the formal question of state sufficiency: given a history space H, a proposed state abstraction F:H->K, and a history-level transformation That:HxI->H, does a corresponding state-level transformation T:KxI->K exist such that F(That(H,i))=T(F(H),i) for all valid H,i -- i.e. do history dynamics descend to the state space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H_A ~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B). Then state sufficiency requires: H_A ~_F H_B => That(H_A,i) ~_F That(H_B,i). Thus ~_F must be a congruence with respect to valid transformations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the equivalence relation ~_F induced by the state abstraction (H_A~_F H_B iff F(H_A)=F(H_B)) and states the central congruence requirement: this equivalence must be preserved by every valid transformation for the state representation to be sufficient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now suppose the proposed state representation retains only Content(K)={p}. ... Authorized(A)=true but Authorized(B)=false. Then F(That(H_A,validate)) != F(That(H_B,validate)). Yet initially F(H_A)=F(H_B). Content-only K fails the congruence test. This is a genuine falsification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies a content-only knowledge state via a worked example: two histories with different evidence sources (A authorized, B not) collapse to the same content-only state, but a governance-sensitive validation transformation produces divergent outcomes (Validated vs Unvalidated) depending on the discarded source information -- a genuine congruence failure, showing content-only K is insufficient once authority-sensitive transformations are valid operations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose we enrich the state with lambda(e)=source(e). Now F(H_A) != F(H_B) ... The previous counterexample disappears. But this does not yet prove sufficiency. We have only shown one missing distinction has been restored.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows adding a source/provenance field lambda(e)=source(e) to the state resolves the specific counterexample found, but explicitly cautions this only restores one missing distinction and does not establish global sufficiency -- more collapsed-but-behaviorally-different histories must still be searched for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose H_C and H_D have identical Content and Provenance. But H_C was produced under policy pi_1 while H_D was produced under pi_2 ... F(H_C)=F(H_D) under a representation that omits policy history. But T(H_C,i) != T(H_D,i). ... Is Policy part of state, provenance, or external context? ... It is de
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a further counterexample: two histories identical in content and provenance but produced under different policies collapse to the same state under a policy-omitting representation, yet future validation depending on the original governing policy produces different results -- concluding whether policy belongs to state, provenance, or external context cannot be decided by convenience but is determined by transformation sufficiency (independently arriving at a question the parallel verifier track, S1602/S1603, was also attacking).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two histories have the same proposition but different validity intervals theta_A(p)=[t0,t1), theta_B(p)=[t1,t2). Suppose a transformation asks CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)? Then the two states produce different results. ... Temporal validity is not merely decorative metadata if temporal queries are
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a temporal-query counterexample (CurrentVersion(S,t1+epsilon)?) that a state representation omitting temporal qualification fails congruence when temporal queries are valid operations -- confirming temporal validity is functionally load-bearing, not decorative metadata.

a_rows_sample.anchor: e1->p and e2->not p. Compare K_A={p,e1} with K_B={p,e1,e2,not p}. A transformation T_assess may produce Assessment(K_A)=Supported but Assessment(K_B)=Conflicted. ... A state representation containing only the latest proposition K={p} would lose information necessary for future assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a contradictory-evidence counterexample showing evidence multiplicity is semantically relevant: two states differing only in whether conflicting evidence is retained produce different Assessment outcomes (Supported vs Conflicted) under T_assess, so a state keeping only the latest proposition would lose information needed for future assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose an information component x can affect the result of a valid future transformation T(K,i). Then x cannot be discarded from the state abstraction unless it is recoverable from other state information. Formally: x is semantically disposable => x=f(K) for some reconstruction function f, or no va
a_rows_sample.statement: States a general disposability criterion generalizing all the preceding counterexamples: an information component x may be discarded from the state abstraction only if it is reconstructible from the remaining state (x=f(K) for some f) or no valid operation can distinguish states differing only in x -- giving a formal test for classifying any candidate field as state, metadata, provenance, external context, or truly redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=F(H) is a transformation-sufficient representation if all permitted future semantics can be determined from K, rather than the complete H. But we should not call K a sufficient statistic without qualification. ... K must be sufficient for the permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws an explicit but qualified analogy to the statistical notion of a sufficient statistic: a state K=F(H) is transformation-sufficient if all permitted KnowledgeOS transformation semantics can be determined from K rather than the full history H -- but the file cautions the statistical term applies to a specific model/parameter and should not be borrowed unqualified, since the KnowledgeOS requirement is broader (sufficiency for a whole permitted transformation semantics, not one parameter).

a_rows_sample.anchor: H ~ mu_H. Then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K = F_* mu_H. ... mu_K is a regime-level object, not necessarily part of K.
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects the state abstraction to measure theory without making it foundational: if H is a random history with distribution mu_H, then K=F(H) induces a push-forward distribution mu_K=F_*mu_H (mu_K(A)=mu_H(F^{-1}(A)) for measurable A); explicitly classifies mu_K as a regime-level object, consistent with the parallel Step 246 finding (S1601) that probability belongs to a regime projection, not to K itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F is a compression map. The question becomes: Is this compression lossless with respect to the semantics we care about? That is exactly the congruence question. ... F o That = T o F. This is the formal expression of state sufficiency.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the commutative-diagram criterion F o That = T o F as the formal expression of state sufficiency (the state abstraction F is a compression map; sufficiency means the compression is lossless with respect to the transformation semantics), calling it one of the strongest formal tests obtained in the corpus so far, and gives the corresponding failure interpretation (a non-commuting diagram means the proposed state representation has lost necessary information).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=(Content,Qualification,Governance) survives the experiments only if those components contain all information required by valid transformations. ... we should not yet assert K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as a final decomposition. Instead: K must be defined by transformation sufficiency. This reverses
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the design question from 'what fields should a Knowledge State have?' to 'what information must a state preserve so that all valid KnowledgeOS transformations remain well-defined?'; explicitly withholds asserting K=(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) as final until it survives transformation-sufficiency testing -- a route to the same skepticism about the 5-tuple that the parallel verifier track reached by counterexample.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Minimality = systematic removal + congruence testing. This is far stronger than selecting the smallest-looking tuple. ... Minimality is always relative to the transformation language. ... Minimality(K) = Minimality(K | T). There may be no context-free 'minimal Knowledge State.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates minimality testing as systematic per-component removal followed by re-checking the congruence criterion (F^{-i} o That = T^{-i} o F^{-i}), rather than choosing the smallest-looking tuple by inspection; states the important architectural corollary that minimality is always relative to the transformation language T (Minimality(K)=Minimality(K|T)) -- there may be no context-free minimal Knowledge State, since a richer future transformation set can make previously-discardable information necessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation-Sufficiency Proposition: T:K x I -> K is semantically well-defined with respect to That iff F(H1)=F(H2) => F(That(H1,i))=F(That(H2,i)) for all valid H1,H2,i. Equivalently F o That = T o F. ... not yet a proven KnowledgeOS theorem, because the full transformation set has not been estab
a_rows_sample.statement: States the phase's central named proposition (Transformation-Sufficiency Proposition), giving a single precise, computationally testable mathematical criterion for when a state-level transformation is semantically well-defined relative to a history-level one -- explicitly labeled not yet a proven theorem because the full KnowledgeOS transformation set has not itself been established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PASS -- Transformation congruence criterion established. FAIL -- Global state sufficiency not yet demonstrated. OPEN -- Minimal sufficient Knowledge State. ... K should not be defined independently of T. Instead, the pair (K,T) must be reconstructed together.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the Step-248 verdict: PASS on establishing the congruence criterion; FAIL on demonstrating global state sufficiency; OPEN on minimal sufficient K; states the phase's major conceptual shift -- K must not be designed independently of the transformation set T, but the pair (K,T) must be reconstructed jointly -- and sets Step 249 as Transformation Algebra Reconstruction, to derive the corpus-supported transformation classes (T_create, T_observe, T_infer, T_validate, T_revise, T_reject, T_merge, T_supersede, ...) with domain/codomain/preconditions/postconditions/invariants/composability for each.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can two states with identical current representation produce different valid future behavior? ... If T(K_A)=K'_A and T(K_B)=K'_B with K'_A not equiv K'_B, then history affects future semantics. In that case, the compressed state K is not sufficient. This gives us a rigorous state sufficiency criteri
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the provenance-metadata-vs-constitutive question into a testable future-behavior criterion avoiding philosophical argument: if two states with identical current representation but different history produce different results under the same transformation, then the state representation is insufficient -- directly the criterion S1608 (Step 248) then executes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose they produce identical lineage edges. Yet the transformations had different policies pi_A != pi_B. If policy is semantically relevant, then lambda_A=lambda_B does not imply H_A = H_B. ... Potentially lambda=(source,transformation,actor,time,policy,evidence). But this is again a candidate str
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies plain parent-child lineage as a sufficient history compression: two histories can produce identical lineage edges while having been governed by different policies, so if policy is semantically relevant then lineage-equality does not imply history-equivalence -- proposing a richer candidate lambda=(source,transformation,actor,time,policy,evidence), still only a candidate structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: That requires: H_1 ~_H H_2 => T(H_1) ~_H T(H_2). This is a congruence condition. If it holds, the transformation descends from histories to states. ... State abstraction is valid only if it is transformation-compatible.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the congruence condition required for the equivalence-class definition of Knowledge State to be usable: ~_H must be preserved by every valid transformation (H1~_H H2 => T(H1)~_H T(H2)), so that transformations descend consistently from histories to their equivalence classes -- directly foreshadowing S1608's F o That = T o F criterion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the smallest mathematical structure that satisfies all non-negotiable requirements? Construct a sequence K0 -> K1 -> K2 -> ... where each added component must have a demonstrated necessity. ... The final result must distinguish MINIMALITY PROVEN from MINIMALITY PLAUSIBLE from MINIMALITY NOT
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a 'minimal adequate K' procedure: build up a sequence K0->K1->K2->... adding only demonstrably-necessary components (tested against 7 questions per candidate: forcing requirement, external representability, derivability, removal breakage, reconstructability, circularity, unwanted coupling), and introduces a 3-level minimality-confidence taxonomy (PROVEN / PLAUSIBLE / NOT ESTABLISHED) explicitly rejecting fewer-fields as a minimality argument -- complementing S1608's congruence-based removal test with a positive constructive procedure.
